docs.text:
Tables budget ceil(students / 2) kits. A final trio gives 5/7/10/12 active teams at 10/15/20/25 pupils; unused eighth/thirteenth team paper/ruler is spare. References to thirteen teams/seven rounds are conservative capacity limits, not required singleton grouping.

  • Per student: 1 evidence half-sheet per meeting (2 total), pencil.
  • Per team: 2 paper sheets per meeting, ruler, paper token, 8 hand-drawn arrow/repeat cards reusable between meetings.
  • Whole class: 2 Sphero robots, 2 compatible devices, 2 chargers, 2 cardboard boundary sets, timer, 4 m floor-safe tape for starts/corners; board. No marker attached to robots.
  • Teacher: pairing/charging access and manufacturer's model instructions. No student charging.
Students Teams Paper sheets across two meetings Half-sheet slips across two meetings Rulers / tokens Arrow/repeat cards Robots / devices / chargers 10 5 20 20 5 each 40 2 each 15 8 32 30 8 each 64 2 each 20 10 40 40 10 each 80 2 each 25 13 52 50 13 each 104 2 each

Students draw cards on their team paper; no elaborate printed kit. Reuse rulers, cards and tokens. With one robot, the teacher demonstrates; log which children actually enter/run code and schedule later operation checks. Do not claim all children operated it.

docs.title: Vocabulary and background
docs.text:
• Sequence: ordered instructions.
  • Loop: repeats enclosed instructions a specified number of times.
  • Heading: direction measured from the robot's aimed reference.
  • Calibration: testing and adjusting settings to match physical movement.
  • Debug: find the difference between expected and actual behavior; change and test.

For a square, four identical rolls use headings 0, 90, 180, 270 in order. A repeat loop around four rolls repeats the whole square; it is not a one-roll square loop. Wheel slip, aim and flooring affect the result.

Misconception: "Correct code guarantees a perfect square." Physical systems vary. Question / answer: "Can it see the tape?" "This lesson does not program line-following. Tape marks our boundary and starting point; we measure and adjust the code."

docs.title: SAFETY
docs.text: Teacher controls pairing, chargers and speed limits. Students stay seated except scheduled operators; only one team enters each area. Roll speed stays at 20 or lower, duration at 1 second or shorter per segment. Stop immediately if a robot leaves the area; retrieve only after motion stops. No collisions as experiments, shaking/throwing, wet floors, or operation near stairs. Keep sound low.

docs.title: Meeting 1: sequence and calibration, exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Purpose and prediction. Original prayer: "God, help us use tools thoughtfully and include each classmate." Ask: "What should happen when we give the same command twice?"
  2. 4-9: Model one roll. Teacher shows paired app, aim, start and stop; run heading 0, speed 20, duration 1 second. Measure actual centimeters. "Which setting is time? Which observation is distance?"
  3. 9-14: Paper rehearsal. On the drawn grid, students trace forward 1 square; forward 1 square; turn right; forward 1 square. One partner reads exactly; the other moves a token. This is a paper algorithm, not Sphero's absolute-heading API.
  4. 14-27: Robot slots and desk work. Teams write a prediction, then in their slot enter two roll blocks at heading 0, speed 20, 1 second each, run and measure endpoint distance from start. Switch operator between entering first and second blocks. Waiting teams predict and trace another paper route. Teacher records names of actual operators; the trio's third child operates in meeting 2.
  5. 27-32: One-change debug. Choose one team result. Change duration only (for example from 1 to 0.5 seconds); predict shorter travel and retest. "What stayed the same? Did it travel exactly half as far?" Do not demand exact proportionality.
  6. 32-35: Individual check. Each child writes/draws the two-command prediction and identifies one adjustment with expected effect. Actual operators also label start/stop and record their measured travel. Mark "paper evidence only" for children without operation.
  7. 35-40: Cleanup and exit. Stop programs, teacher switches off robots and returns paired devices; peel temporary tape without damaging floor, collect tokens/cards, save slips. Ask: "Why record what actually happened, even when it missed our prediction?"

docs.title: Meeting 2: loops and a square, exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-5: Retrieve evidence. "How did duration affect travel?" Review aiming and safe boundaries, not assumed prior expertise.
  2. 5-11: Trace a square. Teacher draws four equal segments. Model roll headings 0, 90, 180, 270, speed 20, 0.5 seconds each. Wait for each roll to finish. Ask: "Why does heading 90 not mean turn 90 more every time?" Point to the fixed direction chart.
  3. 11-16: Represent a repeat. Teams write the four-roll sequence twice, then enclose the four commands in repeat 2. Count 8 rolls. Grade 3 traces once then twice; Grade 4 compares 8 written roll blocks with 4 inside a repeat, saving 4 repeated roll blocks (not all interface blocks).
  4. 16-29: Program/test slots. Teams enter four roll blocks inside a repeat block set to 1 initially; test one square. Change repeat to 2 only if the first stays in bounds. Swap operator from meeting 1. Waiting teams trace the 8-roll paper version. No sensor achievements are claimed.
  5. 29-33: Debug and discuss. "Did it return near start? Which one setting would you adjust?" Teacher retests one shorter duration or re-aimed start; measure endpoint error, not a promised zero.
  6. 33-35: Individual check. Each child shows that repeating four commands twice executes 8 rolls and explains a difference between paper and physical outcomes.
  7. 35-40: Cleanup. Stop, teacher powers off and stores devices; team collects papers/rulers/tokens, restores lanes. Store tested program locally with team ID, not full pupil names.

docs.title: Unplugged / substitute / indoor path
docs.text: Use the same two 40-minute sequences without robots: steps involving app demos become teacher-executed token demos; robot-slot time becomes paired token tracing and one-change debugging. For absolute headings draw north/east/south/west, and define a paper roll as moving one grid square in the named direction. Mark slips CT: sequence/loop/debug; CST-T1 device operation and real distance calibration remain not observed. Weather has no effect; all work is indoor.

docs.title: What success looks like
docs.text: Every child predicts an ordered route, traces a two-repeat sequence as 8 commands, identifies a bug and proposes a retest. Real-device evidence additionally requires that child's observed start/stop or block edit/run and a measured result. Use scores 1 guess only; 2 correct trace with prompts; 3 independent trace and justified debug; 4 explains a physical limitation using data. Record device operation separately; collaboration is not mastery.

docs.title: Troubleshooting and differentiation
docs.text:
• Pairing fails after 2 minutes: announce paper pathway and missing device evidence; do not spend the period resetting accounts.
  • Drift: stop; reset aim/start, shorten duration, change only one setting. Never increase speed to force success.
  • Wrong-direction square: check absolute headings. No triangle/pentagon angle arithmetic is required.
  • Support / Grade 3: read aloud; use 4 arrow cards and a finger/token; partner handles fine-motor input while the child directs and traces.
  • Challenge / Grade 4: compare endpoint errors on two trials and explain why paper tracing does not test traction or Bluetooth.
  • 25 pupils: two test areas, thirteen teams, seven one-minute slots within each thirteen-minute window. No whole-class floor race.

docs.title: Family snippet
docs.text: We used sequences, loops and honest debugging to predict and test routes. Robots add real input/output and calibration; paper work develops computational thinking but is not robot operation. Our Catholic connection was inclusive, responsible tool use. Ask: "What repeats, and what did you change after testing?" Optional at home: give a partner three directions using a paper token. No devices or homework.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Inquiry; one 40-minute meeting. Objective: predict, record three roll distances at each of two ramp heights and explain a fair test. Why/big idea: repeated evidence beats a lucky result. Catholic/CST-C1: report unexpected results truthfully; CST-S1: supported claim; CST-S2: one change/two controls; CST-M1: six readings with cm units. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; developing, ruler use supported. Prep 15 minutes; cleanup 5 included.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Balanced teams <=3: ⅘/7/9. Each kit: smooth 30 cm cardboard ramp, two thin closed books, ball too large to swallow, ruler, catch tray, recording sheet. Per pupil: evidence sheet/pencil. Teacher board/timer; demo uses issued kit. Pretest one- and two-book heights with a clear 60 cm desk lane/tray; shorten ramp if balls escape. Board six trial boxes. Reuse kit; retain records.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Kits; ramps; balls; rulers; trays; team sheets (1/team each) 4 5 7 9 Books (2/team) 8 10 14 18 Evidence sheets; pencils (1/pupil each) 10 15 20 25

docs.title: Vocabulary/background
docs.text: Hypothesis = reasoned testable prediction; variable = changeable feature; trial = repeated test; evidence = recorded result. Measure ramp end to stopped ball; keep ball, lane, release mark and no-push method fixed. Investigations can revisit steps, not follow one rigid recipe. Misconception: higher always means farther. If asked “Why did repeats differ?” Small release/surface differences matter; record spread. Prayer does not guarantee a desired result.

docs.title: SAFETY
docs.text: Low desk only; no throws, hot liquids, chemical hook, tasting or heavy loads. Teacher retrieves floor escapes; stop/report unsafe setups. Indoor primary. The former alternate experiments are not retained.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: “Does ramp height affect distance?” Each predicts with a reason; optional original prayer for honest inquiry.
  2. 4-9: Demonstrate release, catch tray and ruler zero. “What changes? What two conditions must stay the same?”
  3. 9-20: One-book height, three trials; rotate releaser/measurer/recorder.
  4. 20-29: Two-book height, three trials; same lane/ball/release. Circle shortest/longest at each height, no required mean.
  5. 29-35: Each child records six readings, change/two controls and a claim using data. Ask, “Which reading supports or weakens your prediction?”
  6. 35-40: Count tools/balls/books, store ramps, clear trays, collect dated evidence and name one possible next question.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: six cm readings, one change/two controls, evidence-based claim; prediction need not be right. Grade 3/support: marked ruler zero, dictated records. Grade 4/challenge: compare whole-number ranges and overlapping results. Sliding books: reset, label earlier trial invalid, repeat. Short lane: use equal shorter lanes and label capped distances. Missing balls: shared kit with pupil turns; record missing turns explicitly, never invent results. Protect evidence/ cleanup when late.

Family: We repeated a ramp test and reported honest data. Ask, “What stayed the same?” Optional: discuss a testable question, no home experiment.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Structures; two 40-minute meetings. Objective: measure/retest a tower and load-test/retest a plank bridge. Why/big idea: limits make comparisons fair and resources manageable. Catholic/CST-C3: count back stock and justify reuse; CST-E1: criterion/constraint; CST-E2: test/change/retest; CST-M1: cm/count comparisons. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; developing, no prior architecture assumed. Prep 20 minutes with stock; loan acquisition extra. Cleanup 5 per meeting.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Balanced teams <=3: ⅘/7/9. Per team: 30 inspected KEVA planks, ruler, two flat books, ten identical plastic counters, tray. Per pupil: two unit recording sheets/pencil. Teacher board/timer; demo uses issued kit. Pretest an overlapping deck across 8 cm; mark a 20 cm square for towers, 40 cm height cap. Save records, dismantle between meetings. Identical rectangular classroom blocks may replace KEVA for all teams, labeling the substitution.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Kits; rulers; trays (1/team each) 4 5 7 9 Planks (30/team) 120 150 210 270 Books (2/team) 8 10 14 18 Counters (10/team) 40 50 70 90 Recording sheets (2/pupil) 20 30 40 50 Pencils (1/pupil) 10 15 20 25

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: Foundation = base; span = gap; load = test objects; constraint = limit; criterion = performance requirement. Wide bases/overlap may help, not guarantee stability; loose unjoined triangles are not rigid trusses. Misconception: tallest is best. If asked “More weight?” Fixed cap permits comparison, not a dangerous maximum. Desk tests only; no climbing/throwing/ heavy loads/hands below bridges/forced collapses. Stop/report damaged stock. Indoor primary. Religious building imagery is reflection, not structural proof.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: “How can a tower use stock responsibly?” Explain 30-plank limit, 40 cm cap and ten-second unassisted standing criterion.
  2. 4-9: Model base, ruler zero and hands-off test.
  3. 9-20: Each sketches; build tower, rotate builder/measurer/recorder.
  4. 20-30: Record height/time; change base arrangement, rebuild with same allowance, retest. Failed standing trial is evidence.
  5. 30-35: Each child records two heights/pass results, reason for change and reuse choice. “Which observation informed the new base?”
  6. 35-40: Dismantle top-down; count 30 planks, return tools, date records.

docs.title: Meeting 2: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Bridge as access model, not for people; 8 cm gap/30 planks/ten counters.
  2. 4-9: Model overlapping deck; add center counters singly, three-second hold; record last successful count, or “at least ten.”
  3. 9-20: Sketch/build version 1; check book gap/supports.
  4. 20-30: Test, change overlap arrangement, retest with equal span/allowance/ placement. “Where did movement begin?”
  5. 30-35: Each child gives two counts, whole-number difference, kept-same condition and responsible stock choice; no ratios.
  6. 35-40: Remove loads, dismantle/count/store, collect dated records.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets each meeting: criterion/constraint, two measured results, test-backed change and count-back (C3/E1/E2/M1). Grade 3/support: starter base, oral evidence, counting piles of five. Grade 4/challenge: repeat same capped test and explain why “at least ten” is not a maximum. Immediate fall: record zero/widen base. All hold ten: compare arrangement not unsupported strength rankings. Missing stock: equal lower allowance for everyone and stated revised limit; no home purchase. At 25, nine simultaneous desk tests avoid serial queues.

Family: We retested structures and stewarded shared stock. Ask, “Which test informed your change?” Optional: notice a support in a picture.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Service design; three 40-minute meetings. Objective: define a visitor's need, test two sign versions and recommend a revision using evidence. Why: community helpers seek feedback rather than assume another person's needs. Catholic/CST-C2: dignity/access decision; CST-E1: criteria/limits; CST-E2: actual retest; CST-E3: qualified recommendation; CST-A3: critique/revised communication. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; developing. Prep 15 minutes; cleanup 5 per meeting. Classroom prototype, not certified emergency signage or proven benefit.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Board brief: “A visitor needs to find the book-return tray from 1 m away. Use word AND symbol, not color alone.” Select a non-emergency desk destination. Balanced teams <=3: ⅘/7/9; neighboring peer users, three-team exchange when odd. Per team: two cardstock sheets, ruler, two markers, 40 cm tape/unit. Per pupil: three evidence sheets/pencil. Teacher board/timer; demo from issued card, mark 1 m using ruler lengths. No hallway tour/printing.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Teams; rulers (1/team) 4 5 7 9 Cardstock; markers (2/team each) 8 10 14 18 Tape (40 cm/team, cm total) 160 200 280 360 Evidence sheets (3/pupil) 30 45 60 75 Pencils (1/pupil) 10 15 20 25

Save cards/records; reuse tools.

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: User = person using design; prototype = trial version; feedback = actual response; criterion = tested success. Misconception: designer liking proves usefulness. If asked “Will everyone read it?” Peer sample cannot prove universal access; more users are needed before installation. No filters, body-tested aids, shelters or improvised lights. Paper/tape only; no skin tape or private hardship/disability disclosures. Stop/report damaged tools. Indoor primary works in winter.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-5: Brief/prayer for service optional. “What do we know, not assume?”
  2. 5-10: Criterion: identify destination/direction at 1 m within five seconds; constraint: two cards/40 cm tape.
  3. 10-22: Each asks peer “Which word/symbol helps?” Record response, sketch two alternatives; agree on one.
  4. 22-30: Paper mock-up; exchange and record destination/direction correct or not yet, not “looks nice.”
  5. 30-35: Each states need, criterion, constraint, actual comment.
  6. 35-40: Cap/count/store; save dated plans.

docs.title: Meeting 2: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Retrieve feedback without assuming mastery.
  2. 4-9: Model large word/symbol; equal distance/time in tests.
  3. 9-21: Card version 1; every child contributes a purposeful feature.
  4. 21-30: Peer tests twice; record results/confusion and plan one change.
  5. 30-35: Individual feature-purpose diagram and two test results.
  6. 35-40: Save sign/plans, count tools; no real installation.

docs.title: Meeting 3: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: “Which recorded confusion will our revision address?”
  2. 4-9: Critique example: “Arrow unclear at 1 m,” not “bad artist.”
  3. 9-20: Revise on card 2; repeat two equal tests with a neighboring team.
  4. 20-29: Parallel paired presentations; each explains results/tradeoff; three-team exchange rotates listeners within this window.
  5. 29-35: Individual before/after comparison, actual comment and sample limitation; teacher gathers all slips.
  6. 35-40: Count tools/remove test tape/archive. Adult decides display approval.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: user need/limits, real results, critique-backed revision and qualified recommendation. Grade 3/support: pictorial arrow starter/scribing. Grade 4/challenge: readability versus space tradeoff. Unclear sign: simplify one feature/retest. No external partner: label peers as classroom test users. Late: stop decoration, preserve retest/evidence/cleanup. No community outcomes claimed from the model.

Family: We designed a visitor sign and retested it. Ask, “What did a user actually misunderstand?” Optional: discuss a public sign.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Field Teacher information Grade / unit / title Grades 3-4 / Structures / Bridge Engineering Time One meeting, 40 minutes, including cleanup Meaningful domains Catholic service, engineering, mathematics Big idea Changing a bridge's shape can change the load it supports. A failed design gives information, not a judgment about its builder. Student objective "I can test two versions fairly, count the load, and explain one change." Why Engineers use evidence to make connections between places safer and more useful. This is a classroom model, not a bridge for people. Catholic connection Design for people who need access; share materials and report failures honestly. Connecting communities is a service application, not proof of a theological metaphor. Local standards Local program codes, not official standards: CST-C2 (name a user's access need); CST-E1 (state span/load criteria); CST-E2 (test/redesign); CST-M1 (measure/count); CST-M3 (whole-number difference). Technology None; rulers are ordinary classroom tools. No calculators or efficiency ratios required. Difficulty / prerequisites Moderate; count to 20, use a ruler with help, fold paper. Weeks 5-6 provide practice but are not required. Prep / cleanup 15 minutes with ordinary supplies; 5 minutes in class

docs.title: Before class
docs.text:
1. Make pairs; a final trio at odd enrollment. Place two equal-height closed books flat on each tray, with a 15 cm clear gap. Use books at least 20 cm wide.
  2. Put paper, ruler, and 40 cm of tape in each tray. Stack two reserve sheets beside the teacher.
  3. Count 20 identical plastic counters into a cup for each team. Test a flat paper span yourself; stop at 20 even if it survives.
  4. Board: Version | counters held for 3 seconds | shape changed. Draw two supports and a deck. Write the eight time boundaries below. No printing needed.
  5. Record teams and roles: folder/builder and tester/recorder; switch at redesign. The teacher checks gap measurements.

docs.title: Exact supplies
docs.text:
Tables budget ceil(students / 2) kits. With a final trio at odd enrollment, active teams are 5/7/10/12 for 10/15/20/25 pupils; the eighth/thirteenth kit is a spare. Timing allows the larger kit-budget count, not a demand for a child to work alone.

  • Per student: 1 half-sheet evidence slip and 1 pencil.
  • Per team: 2 closed books, 2 sheets of ordinary letter paper, 1 ruler, 40 cm masking tape, 20 identical plastic counters, 1 cup, 1 tray.
  • Whole class: timer, board; 2 reserve paper sheets and 1 spare ruler.
  • Teacher only: scissors to precut tape; no sharp tool distributed.
Students Teams Books Paper including 2 reserves Tape Counters Cups / trays / team rulers Half-sheet slips / pencils 10 5 10 12 sheets 2 m 100 5 each 10 each 15 8 16 18 sheets 3.2 m 160 8 each 15 each 20 10 20 22 sheets 4 m 200 10 each 20 each 25 13 26 28 sheets 5.2 m 260 13 each 25 each

Counters, books, trays, cups and rulers are reusable. Paper and tape are consumable. If fewer counters are available, use the same 10-counter cap for every team and label results "at least 10"; never mix sizes.

docs.title: Vocabulary and teacher background
docs.text:
• Span: open distance between supports.
  • Deck: surface across the gap.
  • Load: objects placed on the deck.
  • Criteria: what a successful design must do.
  • Redesign: change a design using what a test showed.

A fold changes how paper bends. Compare a flat sheet with a sheet folded lengthwise into an accordion; do not promise that every folded version will win. Here we test a beam-like paper bridge, not all four bridge types. Supports must stay still.

Common misconception: "More counters always means a better design." Not if the span, counter size, or placement changed.

If a student asks: "Why did it fall?" Answer: "The load bent or moved the paper or supports. Point to the first part that changed, then choose a shape change to test."

docs.title: SAFETY
docs.text: Build on desks, over trays, with supports flat and low. No standing on furniture, throwing loads, heavy weights, or loading above 20 counters. Keep fingers out from beneath loaded paper. No coins, loose metal washers, or food. Never test a model with a person or pet.

docs.title: Numbered lesson sequence: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Need and purpose. "Who might need a bridge to reach school or a clinic?" Offer a fictional map of a stream. Short original prayer: "God, help us use careful work to serve our neighbors." State the 15 cm gap and 20-counter cap.
  2. 4-8: Model the fair test. Lay one flat sheet across the books, overlapping each support. Put counters one at a time at the center, wait 3 seconds after each. Count only the last load that stayed for 3 seconds. If collapse occurs on counter 7, record 6. Ask: "What must stay the same next time?" Answer sought: gap, paper amount, counters, placement and waiting time.
  3. 8-12: Plan. Each student draws a first shape and predicts a whole-number load. Partners agree on one version. Use one sheet per version; tape allowance is 20 cm each. No tape to books or desk.
  4. 12-20: Build version 1. Teams fold or roll one sheet, place it, and check the gap. "Where does the load push the paper?" Give a flat-sheet starter to a stuck team. Recording predictions does not require correct guesses.
  5. 20-25: Test version 1. Tester places counters; recorder counts. Tests occur simultaneously at desks after the teacher's signal. Record last successful count and where bending started. If 20 holds, write at least 20, not "maximum 20."
  6. 25-31: Change and retest. Swap roles. Use sheet 2; change shape only. Keep span and load method fixed. Test again. "Did the result support your prediction? What did you change?"
  7. 31-35: Individual evidence. On the slip: draw the changed shape; write both counts; calculate the whole-number change. Example: 6 then 11 means 5 more. A child may dictate while pointing to their table. Ask each child, not only the spokesperson: "What stayed the same?"
  8. 35-40: Explain, clean, exit. Two teams share different outcomes. Explain that a failure is useful evidence. Students count counters into cups, remove tape, flatten paper for recycling where accepted, return rulers/books, and wipe dry trays. Teacher collects slips during cleanup and records missing evidence for follow-up.

docs.title: What success looks like
docs.text:
Each child identifies a kept-same condition, records two actual load counts (or capped lower bounds), and explains a shape change with evidence. Grade 3 compares by addition/subtraction within 20; no mass-per-piece, decimal division, or efficiency ratio. Grade 4 also describes why a capped result cannot establish a maximum; optional equal-material comparisons use whole numbers only.

Quick score: 1 unsupported claim; 2 two counts with help but no fair-test explanation; 3 two counts, correct comparison, kept-same condition and redesign reason; 4 level 3 plus explains a limitation or proposes a fair repeat. A beautiful bridge alone is not mastery.

docs.title: Troubleshooting: if things go wrong
docs.text:
• Immediate collapse: record 0; show an accordion fold and test it. Do not erase the failed trial.
  • Supports slide: reset, mark their edges with pencil on scrap paper, repeat; label the earlier trial invalid.
  • All bridges hold 20: compare shapes, not unsupported claims about strength. Retest at the same cap if time remains.
  • Not enough books: use two identical stable low blocks per team, or share support trays between two neighboring teams; plan/build at each desk and stagger tests within the same test windows.
  • Finished early: repeat the same test and note whether the count agrees.

docs.title: Support, challenge, indoor alternative
docs.text:
Support / Grade 3: teacher models one accordion fold; use tally marks and oral explanation; partners stabilize materials, never the bridge during a test. Provide folded paper for fine-motor access without taking away the test decision.

Challenge / Grade 4: compare two trials of the same version and explain variation; do not introduce ratios as the expected task. A trio rotates builder, loader and recorder; every child completes evidence.

Indoor alternative: this lesson is already indoor and independent of Minnesota weather.

docs.title: Family snippet: this week in C-STREAM
docs.text: We tested and improved paper bridges with the same span and load method. Each child used whole-number evidence to explain a redesign. Our Catholic connection was designing access for neighbors and sharing resources responsibly. Ask: "What changed, and what stayed the same?" Optional at home: point out a bridge in a picture and discuss who it serves. No building supplies, devices, purchases, or homework required.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Gratitude; one 40-minute meeting. Objective: edit/run two ordered Scratch messages and revise for a reader. Why: actual execution exposes order/timing errors. Catholic/CST-C2: respectful thanks without private disclosure; CST-T1 actual edit/run/stop; CST-T2 sequence/debug; CST-A3 critique/revised message. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology Required for executed code; introductory, no Scratch prerequisite. Prep 20 minutes after software works; installation extra. Cleanup 5 included.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Scratch 3 guest/offline, no accounts. Preflight blank project: assemble below, run twice, Stop, save local .sb3, reopen. Leave working sample/save location with substitute. Failed preflight means paper path/report missing operation. Balanced teams <=3 (⅘/7/9), computer/team; paper/pencil per pupil. Teacher board/timer, demo from issued device; devices reusable, paper retained.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Computers (1/team) 4 5 7 9 Paper; pencils (1/pupil each) 10 15 20 25

docs.title: Starter, vocabulary and background
docs.text:
One sprite, Code tab; connect blocks:

when green flag clicked
say [Thank you, classroom helpers.] for (2) seconds
say [You keep our space ready.] for (2) seconds

Event = trigger; sequence = ordered actions; sprite = programmed character; debug = fix mismatch. Misconception: timed message remains after Stop. If asked “Need broadcasts?” Not for one sprite's sequence; learn a small working program first. Human moral judgment is not an automatic coded rule.

docs.title: SAFETY / privacy
docs.text: Dry seated devices; no names/photos/voices, passwords, downloads or public delivery. Stop/report damaged leads or access failures. Fictional/classroom thanks allowed; feelings/prayer not graded. Indoor primary.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: “How can thanks name a helpful action?” Optional original prayer for respectful communication.
  2. 4-10: Demo starter/flag/Stop. “Which message appears first?”
  3. 10-21: Each pupil has three-minute edit/run turn: replace message, predict order, run/record. Peers plan/read for clarity.
  4. 21-29: Peer reads messages, gives specific feedback; change text/duration and rerun. “Was there enough reading time?”
  5. 29-35: Individual two-step trace and critique-backed change; roster logs actual edit/run/stop separately.
  6. 35-40: Stop/save/reopen check, return devices, collect dated paper.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: correct trigger/trace, observed operation and specific message revision. Grade 3/support: copy starter/dictation/motor assistance. Grade 4/challenge: add one-second wait and predict timing. Not running: correct sprite, hat and block attachment; rerun. Fewer devices: two waves of three-minute turns within work windows; below half required stations use paper/reschedule, not rushed turns. No device/internet: paper event/two-message cards at same times; CT/art only, Scratch operation not observed. No home completion.

Family: We executed and revised gratitude messages. Ask, “What triggered the sequence?” Optional: say a thanks, no home coding.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Service design; one 40-minute meeting. Objective: design a page marker for a reader, test twice and revise one feature. Why/big idea: a gift serves a stated need rather than its price. Catholic/CST-C2: listen to recipient; CST-E1: function/size criteria; CST-E2: actual before/after tests; CST-A2: visual choice supports use. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; introductory. Prep 10 minutes; cleanup 5 included.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Adult cuts two 5 x 15 cm cardstock blanks per pupil; one is a revision spare. Each pupil gets one paper evidence sheet/pencil. Teams <=3 (⅘/7/9) share one closed classroom book, two markers and blunt scissors. Check book edges/cards; demo from issued blank. Teacher board/timer; no lamination/gift templates. Book/tools reusable; card consumable; save evidence.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Card blanks (2/pupil) 20 30 40 50 Paper; pencils (1/pupil each) 10 15 20 25 Books; scissors (1/team each) 4 5 7 9 Markers (2/team) 8 10 14 18

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: User = reader; function = job; prototype = trial; contrast = visible difference. Criterion: protrudes above closed book by at least 2 cm and permits finding the marked page twice. Misconception: beauty alone proves function. If asked “Does it have to cost money?” Thoughtful time/attention can serve. Catholic generosity is application, not a claim that this gift guarantees joy. No blades, laminator, string tassels, food or private photos. Seated scissors; stop/report damaged edges. Indoor primary; no recipient delivery without adult consent, and paper gift only.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Optional prayer for generous work. “What does a reader need?”
  2. 4-9: Model placement/protrusion/two retrieval tests; ask a peer which symbol would help. Fictional recipient allowed.
  3. 9-21: Each makes marker with visible top symbol and brief encouraging original message; explain color/form choice to peer.
  4. 21-30: Test locating page twice; record results, revise top/placement or contrast and retest twice. Do not glue anything into book.
  5. 30-35: Each child shows need, criterion, before/after record and visual choice.
  6. 35-40: Cap/count tools, return books, collect dated evidence; approved paper gifts may go home, no compulsory recipient response.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: stated user need, two versions actually tested, criterion checked and purposeful visual explanation (C2/E1/E2/A2). Grade 3/support: pre-cut blank, picture message, scribing. Grade 4/challenge: compare readability without relying only on color. Marker buried: adjust placement/shape, not thicker book damage. No book: folded paper booklet for every team, label model test. Early finish: try another book and explain limits. Missing feedback recorded, not invented.

Family: We made functional gifts and tested a page marker. Ask, “What changed after the test?” Optional: discuss what makes a thoughtful gift.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Portfolio; one 40-minute meeting. Objective: explain one artifact using actual evidence, demonstrate its reasoning again and revise a display caption after feedback. Why/big idea: celebrating growth is more informative than ranking favorite decorations. Catholic/CST-C3: gifts used responsibly, inventory care; CST-E3: evidence/limit in explanation; CST-A3: audience critique/caption revision. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; developing. Prep 10 minutes; cleanup 5 included. Celebration is not an all-domain mastery certificate.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Return each child's portfolio; identify an earlier plan/test record, not only a photo. Missing portfolios use a fresh paper-tower evidence task below, labeled today rather than invented growth. Per pupil: portfolio, two paper sheets (caption/evidence and demonstration), pencil. Teams <=3 (⅘/7/9) share ruler. Teacher board/timer, prompt written large. All share at desks, no four-device station rotation, food or awards requiring extra time.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Portfolios; pencils (1/pupil each) 10 15 20 25 Paper (2/pupil) 20 30 40 50 Rulers (1/team) 4 5 7 9

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: Artifact = saved work; evidence = recorded result; caption = explanatory label; reflection = reasoned look back. Misconception: attendance proves skill. If asked "Am I a master coder?" Only observed individual operation supports that skill; a paper trace is a different kind of evidence. Dry paper displays; no restarted robots/circuits, small prizes, balloons or private pupil photos. Report missing/broken supplies. Indoor primary.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Optional prayer of thanks; "Which work shows a decision you changed?"
  2. 4-9: Model caption: task, real result, reason, limit; distinguish measured from predicted and actually operated from watched.
  3. 9-19: Select artifact and caption it. Each independently re-explains a test or code trace. Missing artifact: fold a standing paper tower, measure cm and ten-second standing, then change base/retest, recording today's evidence.
  4. 19-29: Parallel team round: each has two minutes to explain/demonstrate; peers ask "What evidence supports that?" Give one specific caption suggestion.
  5. 29-35: Each revises caption and submits artifact reference plus fresh explanation/limit and material-care choice; teacher checks individual slips.
  6. 35-40: Date/store portfolios, count rulers, collect captions and clear desks. Gratitude may be private; enthusiasm not scored.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: identifiable evidence, fresh reasoning demonstration, accurate limitation, caption revision and responsible return. Grade 3/support: point/dictate; two caption stems. Grade 4/challenge: compare two dated artifacts and identify what cannot be inferred. Unsupported caption: change "proved" to evidence-supported claim, never fabricate data. No earlier artifact: today's demonstration only, not year-growth certification. Early finish: revise for a new reader.

Family: We celebrated learning with evidence and revised captions. Ask, "Which result supports your explanation?" Optional: listen to the explanation.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Light; two 40-minute meetings. Objective: record reflected/refracted light observations and revise a transmitting Advent composition after a same-distance test. Why: optics helps explain tools/windows; purposeful art communicates hope. Catholic/CST-C1: distinguish measured light from religious symbolism; CST-S1: observations; CST-S3: light-path model; CST-A2: purposeful composition; CST-A3: critique/revision. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None, but physical flashlights required; introductory. Prep 15 minutes plus adult battery check; cleanup 5 per meeting.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Teams <=3 (⅘/7/9). Each kit: enclosed flashlight, acrylic mirror, uncut clear plastic cup, tray, three tissue squares, cardstock sheet, glue stick. Per pupil: two recording sheets/pencil. Teacher board/timer and 50 mL water per team, poured by adult only in meeting 1; demo uses issued kit. Class: one graduated plastic pouring cup and one roll of towels for drying/spills. Check secured batteries/no cracked mirrors; pretest mirror aiming onto desk paper and pencil appearance through water. Adult cuts a window in cardstock before meeting 2; keep room normally lit. Dry kits before storage.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Kits; flashlights; mirrors; cups; trays; cardstock; glue (1/team each) 4 5 7 9 Tissue squares (3/team) 12 15 21 27 Water (50 mL/team, mL total) 200 250 350 450 Recording sheets (2/pupil) 20 30 40 50 Pencils (1/pupil) 10 15 20 25 Graduated cup; towel roll (fixed each) 1 1 1 1

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: Reflection = light changes direction at a surface; refraction = change of direction between materials; transmission = passage through; composition = arrangement conveying meaning. Misconception: pencil is actually bent. If asked "Is spiritual light measurable?" No; Advent light is a religious symbol, not a lux reading. No flames, glass, lasers, sun-viewing, loose cells or fully dark rotations. Beam onto desks, never eyes. Adult handles batteries/ water; stop/dry spills and report damaged kit. Indoor flashlight tests do not depend on daylight. No unverified liturgical/saint claims needed.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: "How can light change direction?" Optional prayer for careful inquiry.
  2. 4-10: Model desk mirror target, water-pencil observation and safe beam.
  3. 10-22: Every pupil aims mirror once and draws source/mirror/target arrows. Adult pours water; each draws pencil dry then viewed through water.
  4. 22-30: Repeat from a second viewing angle; compare appearance and explain that a picture models light, not a real bent pencil.
  5. 30-35: Individual reflection/refraction observations and symbol-versus- measurement distinction; "Which evidence showed a change?"
  6. 35-40: Adult empties cups; dry/count/store, collect dated sheets.

docs.title: Meeting 2: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Review observations; Advent preparation/hope is the faith application.
  2. 4-9: Show tissue/window frame; flashlight always 20 cm behind frame.
  3. 9-21: Design three-panel composition using tissue; each pupil explains one placement/color choice communicating hope, not just decoration.
  4. 21-30: Peer identifies intended shape at 1 m; record correct/not yet, revise one overlap or outline and retest at same light/view distance.
  5. 30-35: Each draws path through tissue, records two results and explains critique-backed visual choice and religious/scientific distinction.
  6. 35-40: Switch off/count equipment, save paper art, cap glue/clear desks.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: two accurate optical observations/path, explicit symbolic distinction and test-backed visual revision. Grade 3/support: trace arrows, oral explanation, precut window. Grade 4/challenge: explain overlapping layers/readability tradeoff. No visible reflection: reset angle onto closer paper, not eyes. No water: reflection/transmission only; refraction not observed. Missing flashlight: share between neighboring teams within work windows; never infer operation from watching. No home hardware.

Family: We investigated light and revised Advent art. Ask, "Which part was science and which was a symbol?" Optional: notice a safe light source.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Astronomy; one 40-minute meeting. Objective: construct/measure a not-to-scale sky model, show a pattern and distinguish observation from interpretation. Why: models reveal relationships but cannot identify the Christmas star. Catholic/CST-C1: honest claim limits, Magi as religious narrative; CST-S3: model/limit; CST-A1: two labeled views; CST-M1: three cm positions/comparison. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; introductory. Prep 10; cleanup 5 included.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Teams <=3 (⅘/7/9); kit ruler and three cardstock markers labeled X/Y/Z. Per pupil: two paper sheets/pencil. Teacher board/timer, draw side view positions 10/20/30 cm and front-view star dots. No star chart, biography or astronomical distance claim needed. Demo from issued kit. Cards/rulers reusable, records saved.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Rulers (1/team) 4 5 7 9 Markers (3/team) 12 15 21 27 Paper (2/pupil) 20 30 40 50 Pencils (1/pupil) 10 15 20 25

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: Star = self-luminous astronomical object; planet = orbiting body, visible here by reflected light; constellation = recognized sky pattern; model = selective representation. Our Sun is a star. A flat pattern does not show actual star distances. Misconception: neighboring dots mean neighboring stars in space. If asked "Was the Christmas star a comet?" This lesson does not establish its physical identity. The Magi narrative is religious interpretation, not our experiment. No inherited firsts/saint labels or speculative travel distances. Paper desk work; no Sun observation, laser or required night outing. Stop/report damaged rulers; indoor primary works through Minnesota winter.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: "Can a drawing tell us everything about the sky?" Optional prayer for wonder and truthful inquiry; paraphrase Magi seeking/worshiping.
  2. 4-10: Draw three front-view dots, then side view; label not to scale.
  3. 10-22: Every pupil places/measures markers at 10/20/30 cm and draws side/front views. Rotate tools; compare near/far and whole-number differences.
  4. 22-30: Move Y to 25 cm, redraw side view; discuss how similar-looking sky patterns can hide different depths. "What did the model omit?"
  5. 30-35: Each child submits three measurements, labeled model limit and two statements: one observable in model, one religious interpretation.
  6. 35-40: Count cards/rulers, save dated views, clear desks.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: three cm readings, two intelligible views, one model limitation and correct claim distinction (C1/S3/A1/M1). Grade 3/support: marked positions, pointing/dictation. Grade 4/challenge: explain how perspective confounds a distance guess; no light-year calculation. Unclear front view: teacher draws projected dots rather than asking pupils to crouch at desk edges. Missing ruler: shared ruler turns, record positions actually checked. Early finish: propose what real astronomical evidence would be needed.

Family: We compared model views and honest limits. Ask, "Does a sky pattern show depth?" Optional: look at a sky picture, no outdoor/night homework.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Reflection; one 40-minute meeting. Objective: write one achievable classroom goal, perform two practice checks and use counts to choose a next action. Why/big idea: a tracker informs practice, not promises success. Catholic/CST-C3: stewardship of effort/materials; CST-M2: two labeled trial records; CST-M3: count/compare achieved criteria. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; introductory. Prep 10 minutes; cleanup 5 included. No prayer/holiness score.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Per pupil: two sheets/pencil. Teams <=3 (⅘/7/9) share ruler. Board SMART: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound. Draw a 2 cm line example. Practice goal: "By minute 30 I will label a drawing with a title, cm unit and measured line length: three checked features." Teacher board/timer, demo uses issued paper. Evidence requires no calendars/printed template.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Paper (2/pupil) 20 30 40 50 Pencils (1/pupil) 10 15 20 25 Rulers (1/team) 4 5 7 9

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: Specific = clear action; measurable = observable count; achievable = realistic; tracker = dated evidence record. SMART is a planning tool, not a guarantee. Misconception: many goals ensure more growth. If asked "Does missing a goal mean God is disappointed?" A practice result tells us what support/ next action to try; it does not measure a person's worth or faith. Desk paper/rulers; no speed pressure, private faith/family disclosure or compulsory daily tracking. Report broken tools; indoor primary.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Optional prayer for patient growth. "How would we know 'get better' happened?" Explain one practice goal, not three private goals.
  2. 4-10: Model SMART and tracker trial/time | features 0-3 | next action.
  3. 10-20: Each writes goal/reason/two actions; draws and labels first measured line. Peer checks title/unit/value; pupil records actual 0-3 count.
  4. 20-30: Choose action from missing feature, draw different length line, check three features again and compare counts. Deadline is this window.
  5. 30-35: Each child explains goal, two actual checks, count difference and next action; "Which action responded to your evidence?"
  6. 35-40: Date/file tracker, count rulers, clear desks; teacher notes who needs reteaching. Optional next-class check uses tracker during opening, not hidden additional required instruction.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: one SMART goal, two real 0-3 records and evidence-based next action with responsible work choice. Grade 3/support: copy goal, oral/dictated reason. Grade 4/challenge: explain why one successful attempt does not establish durable skill and propose a later check. Unrealistic goal: shorten to today's three features, not five projects. No change in counts: explain maintenance or missing support; do not invent improvement. Early finish: change line length, same rubric.

Family: We practiced one measurable goal and compared checks. Ask, "What did your tracker change about your next step?" Optional conversation only.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Choice inquiry; four 40-minute meetings. Objective: conduct a common shadow test, choose a prepared project, manage stock and use repeated feedback to revise a final explanation/performance. Why: independent choice needs a testable question, not unspecified stations. Catholic/CST-C3: steward talents/time; CST-S2: common controlled shadow test; CST-E2: project test/revision; CST-A3: visual/musical critique and revision; CST-M1: common cm measurements plus counted beats/lengths. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; ordinary flashlight physically required for shadow inquiry. Developing; no electronics, chemistry, autonomous robotics or advanced Scratch options retained. Prep 20 minutes; cleanup 5 each meeting.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Balanced teams <=3 (⅘/7/9). Per team/unit: enclosed flashlight, two cardstock sheets (standing screen and silhouette), ruler, 60 cm tape. Per pupil: four passport sheets/pencil. Teacher board/timer; demo uses issued kit. Pretest desk light at 10/20 cm from same silhouette/screen; normal room lighting. Write two complete choice cards:

  • Shadow story: three silhouette arrangements communicate "welcome/help/ thanks"; test reader's interpretation, no scientific claim from symbolism.
  • Rhythm message: four-beat welcome pattern using quiet desk taps or gestures; listener repeats it, revise for clarity. No loud instruments or faith ranking.

All pupils do the common science test before choosing; no station movement.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Teams; lights; rulers (1/team each) 4 5 7 9 Cardstock (2/team) 8 10 14 18 Tape (60 cm/team, cm total) 240 300 420 540 Passport sheets (4/pupil) 40 60 80 100 Pencils (1/pupil) 10 15 20 25

Reuse tools/silhouettes, retain passports; tape consumable.

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: Variable = changed feature; silhouette = outline; beat = steady pulse; iteration = tested revision. Shadow size depends on geometry, not only object size. Music communicates through purposeful rhythm, not volume. Misconception: choice means no plan. If asked "Can I invent another lab?" Not today; these two have supplies/tests ready. No flames, laser, dark-room walking, loose cells or skin tape. Lights onto screens, never eyes; adult battery handling. Report damaged gear. Quiet/seated gestures and indoor primary.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Optional prayer for stewardship; introduce both choices/passport.
  2. 4-10: Model fixed screen/silhouette, change only light distance 10/20 cm.
  3. 10-22: Every child measures shadow width at each distance; rotate roles, repeat both readings and record cm with two controls.
  4. 22-30: Try one shadow phrase and one four-beat rhythm; select project using a reason and criterion: reader identifies phrase/listener repeats beat.
  5. 30-35: Individual four readings/controls, choice/stock-use plan.
  6. 35-40: Off/count/store, save passport.

docs.title: Meeting 2: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Retrieve choice/question and remaining stock.
  2. 4-9: Model trial log attempt | response | change.
  3. 9-21: Build three-image sequence OR compose/notate four-beat pattern; every child authors a part and practices.
  4. 21-30: Neighbor tests twice without being told intended answer; record correct/not yet and specific visual/rhythmic feedback.
  5. 30-35: Individual explanation of two results and planned revision.
  6. 35-40: Count/save; passport records actual supply use.

docs.title: Meeting 3: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: "What evidence makes this change worth trying?"
  2. 4-9: Model one changed visual feature or beat pause, keeping task length.
  3. 9-21: Revise chosen project; repeat two equal reader/listener tests.
  4. 21-30: Compare results; every child performs/shows revised part; prepare explanation distinguishing science findings from artistic meaning.
  5. 30-35: Individual before/after, quantity comparison and stewardship choice.
  6. 35-40: Store/off/count, no required home finishing.

docs.title: Meeting 4: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Review final criterion; no all-domain certification.
  2. 4-9: Model claim supported by passport, plus sample limitation.
  3. 9-20: Final two tests with a new neighboring reader/listener; record.
  4. 20-29: Parallel team showcase, two minutes per child; feedback specific to meaning/rhythm, not artistic talent.
  5. 29-35: Each submits four-meeting passport, common science claim and critique-backed artistic revision/limit.
  6. 35-40: Return/count stock, flatten reusable silhouettes, archive work.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: common four readings/controls, repeated project tests and deliberate artistic revision with responsible stock use. Grade 3/support: two shadow shapes or four pictured beats, scribing. Grade 4/challenge: explain sample limits/tradeoff between complexity and readability. Weak shadows: closer screen, repeat equal geometry. No light: common test teacher-led with individual turns; otherwise model reasoning only, physical inquiry not observed. Rhythm access: gesture instead of sound, same repeat criterion. Early finish: new listener, not an unprepared hazardous lab. All work indoors.

Family: We chose prepared science/art projects, including rhythm, and revised using evidence. Ask, "What did feedback change?" Optional: repeat four quiet beats.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Faith and evidence; one 40-minute meeting. Objective: support one heritage fact with its source, explain four groups of three with a diagram and revise the explanation using a reader's feedback. Why: Catholic education joins truthful source use, mathematical clarity and knowledge used in service. CST-C1 history/classroom-evidence distinction; CST-T3 source/credit; CST-A3 visual explanation/critique/revision; CST-M3 whole-number grouping and justified total. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; introductory, count to twelve with support. Prep 15 minutes first use, 10 with prepared cards; cleanup 5 included.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Use the Agnesi card in verified Catholic scientific heritage. Prepare two half-sheet cards per team <=3 (⅘/7/9), from one ordinary sheet:

  1. Heritage card: original read-aloud from that resource: "Agnesi wrote a mathematics book intended to make ideas easier to learn. Later she devoted herself to caring for people in need. Clear explanations and service are valuable uses of knowledge." Source: University of St Andrews MacTutor biography, scholarly institutional secondary history, directly checked October 4,
  2. This is our teacher paraphrase, not an attributed Agnesi quotation.
  3. Classroom task card: "A classroom has four trays with three markers in each. Show a new learner how to find the total." Draw four boxes with three marks each. This is an original classroom example, not a quotation or numerical example taken from Agnesi's book.

Each pupil receives two sheets/pencil; each team shares two markers/card pair. Teacher board/timer; demo uses issued paper. Reuse cards. No printer requirement: write these two cards once on the board and read aloud if copies are unavailable.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Source/task cards; markers (2/team each) 8 10 14 18 Card preparation paper (1/team) 4 5 7 9 Pupil paper (2/pupil) 20 30 40 50 Pencils (1/pupil) 10 15 20 25

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: Source = where a historical claim comes from; group = equal collection; worked example = shown reasoning; revision = change that clarifies meaning. Four groups of three total twelve: 3+3+3+3=12. Multiplication notation is optional; the diagram/reasoning is the evidence. Misconception: an attractive diagram proves correct arithmetic. If asked "Was Agnesi the first woman professor?" That claim is not taught; the scholarly source distinguishes an appointment from actual teaching. No inferred personal motivation or invented saint/faith quotation. Paper work indoors, no public research accounts, private media or service delivery. Report damaged markers; no real marker-stock total is inferred.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: "How can clear knowledge serve a learner?" Optional original prayer for truthful, generous work. Read the short Agnesi card.
  2. 4-10: Identify institution/source type; separate heritage fact, classroom example and faith application. Model counting one group, not the full answer.
  3. 10-22: Each child cites one supported fact, draws four groups of three and explains the total with repeated addition or counting. Give the diagram a purposeful title/labels so another learner can follow it.
  4. 22-30: Peer names the groups and explains the total without coaching. Record an actual question/comment; correct any arithmetic and revise one visual feature or explanatory sentence. Retest with the same four groups.
  5. 30-35: Each child shows a sourced fact, correct twelve-object diagram/ reasoning and feedback-backed before/after explanation. Ask, "Which fact came from history, and which result did you work out?"
  6. 35-40: Cap/count tools, retain dated diagrams/cards, clear desks.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: supported fact/citation, four equal groups with total twelve and justified calculation, specific communication revision and source distinction. Biography recall alone is insufficient. Grade 3/support: four drawn boxes, counting marks/read-aloud/scribing. Grade 4/challenge: compare three groups of four with four groups of three and explain the same total; no ratios/decimals. Missing cards: use the complete board text above. Wrong total: recount each group and correct the written reasoning, not just decoration. Unclear diagram: revise labels/spacing from the actual reader comment. Early finish: a different reader explains the same example. No required home research.

Family: We used a sourced heritage example, then explained mathematics and revised for a learner. Ask, "What made your explanation clearer?" Optional: explain the four groups verbally; no purchase or homework.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Computing; two 40-minute meetings. Objective: implement a score variable/condition, predict four inputs and debug/retest restart and boundary behavior. Why: execution reveals whether rules work at their limits. Catholic/CST-C2: clear accessible play rules, no ranking people's worth by scores; CST-T1 actual operation; CST-T2 condition/ debugging; CST-M3 counts 0-3. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology Required; novice starter provided, not dependent on Year B. Prep 20 after Scratch 3 works; installation extra; cleanup 5 each.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Guest/offline Scratch; create Score for all sprites, one target sprite. Preflight full starter below, clicks and space separately, reset/local save/ reopen. Leave known-good sample and save location. Team <=3 computer and three plastic counters; each pupil two paper sheets/pencil. Teacher board/timer/demo uses issued device. Paper/counters available for failed preflight.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Computers (1/team) 4 5 7 9 Counters (3/team) 12 15 21 27 Paper (2/pupil) 20 30 40 50 Pencils (1/pupil) 10 15 20 25

docs.title: Complete starter, vocabulary and background
docs.text:
Connect four stacks on the target:

when green flag clicked
set [Score] to (0)
say [Click me or press space. Three points ends scoring.]

when this sprite clicked
broadcast [point] and wait

when [space] key pressed
broadcast [point] and wait

when I receive [point]
if <(Score) < (3)> then
  change [Score] by (1)
end
if <(Score) = (3)> then
  say [Three reached. Green flag restarts.]
end

Variable = stored value; condition = test; event = trigger; boundary = limit. Use distinct taps, not held keys or simultaneous inputs. Expected trace: 0,1,2,3,3; restart 0. Misconception: continuous touching is one point. If asked "Why not a catch game?" Continuous contact requires extra guarding; discrete input makes this novice rule testable. Human ethics is not an if block.

docs.title: SAFETY/privacy
docs.text: Dry seated devices, private local files; no accounts/media/public upload. Counters stay on desks, away from mouthing pupils. Stop/report damaged cables. Indoor primary; hardware stays at school.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: "What should the fourth input do?" Explain fair, readable rules.
  2. 4-10: Demo variable creation, blocks and trace using counters.
  3. 10-22: Build starter; every pupil edits/runs for three minutes while peers predict/record. No ready-made file purchase.
  4. 22-30: Four distinct clicks then restart; record predicted/actual values; debug disconnected hat/wrong variable, rerun.
  5. 30-35: Individual trace/guard explanation; log actual edit/run separately.
  6. 35-40: Stop/save/reopen, return devices/counters, collect dated records.

docs.title: Meeting 2: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Recall boundary/reset without assuming mastery.
  2. 4-9: Demonstrate equal single-input tests and keyboard access.
  3. 9-21: Every pupil tests four space taps and reset; each edits one rule message for accessibility, not the cap.
  4. 21-30: Peer plays using displayed rules, records confusion; revise message and repeat click/space boundary/reset tests.
  5. 30-35: Each explains original bug/correction or verified no-bug result, two test traces and access choice. "What stayed three?"
  6. 35-40: Stop/save, count/store, file dated evidence.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: correct trace/condition/reset plus observed edit/run and rule revision. Grade 3/support: copied stacks, counter trace, scribing. Grade 4/challenge: explain <3 versus <=3 on paper then restore/test proper guard. Score jumps: check duplicate receive stacks, use one input at a time. Missing device: paper event/condition/counter trace at same times; CT/math only, executed Scratch not observed. Below full capacity, half stations permit two waves of three-minute turns; otherwise reschedule operation. Early finish: test limit again, not unsafe or unguarded catch-game expansion.

Family: We executed bounded scores and restart tests. Ask, "Why did the fourth input stay three?" Optional: explain the rule without a device.

docs.title: Weeks 26-27: Snap Circuits - Build, Test & Design
Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Field Teacher information Grade / unit Grades 3-4 / Circuits Time Two 40-minute meetings, including 5-minute cleanup in each Domains Catholic inclusive design, science systems, technology tools, engineering Big idea A switch controls a light by opening/closing a complete conducting path. Student objective "I can trace and test a switched light, then improve its classroom label using evidence." Why Safe troubleshooting and clear signals help people use shared tools. Catholic connection Each person has dignity regardless of a successful build. Give everyone a real turn and design a label that includes readers with different needs; cooperation is not proof that people function like circuit parts. Local standards Local, not official: CST-C2 (access decision), CST-S3 (return-path model), CST-T1 (safe test/repair), CST-E1 (criteria/constraints), CST-E2 (before/after redesign). Technology None: no computer, app or programming. Approved electrical hardware is required for actual circuit evidence; paper does not demonstrate electrical operation. Prerequisites No previous electronics required; teacher introduces open/closed now. Prep / cleanup First inspection 30 minutes; repeat prep 15 minutes; missing instructions/approval extra. Cleanup 5 minutes per meeting included.

docs.title: Before class
docs.text: Use the OLP Snap Circuits guide. Complete every model/instructions/age/power preflight gate before releasing the hardware route. Select the matching manufacturer's simple battery/slide-switch/ lamp project and leave its diagram and component list with the kits. No assumed dimmer, motion/sound sensor, automatic night light, motor or fan. The filename is retained for existing links; LittleBits color-chain directions are not instructions for a Snap circuit.

docs.title: Exact supplies
docs.text:
• Per pupil: pencil, one evidence sheet used across both meetings.
  • Per team: one diagram sheet, one cardstock label, ruler, shared marker; one dry work area. No extra mounting base: keep the circuit on its supplied grid.
  • Hardware station: one preflight-approved Snap Circuits STEM Classroom Activity Kit (OHM-135) with only the selected project's parts and one tray.
  • Teacher/class: approved instructions/setup card, board, timer, roster, adult-controlled cells and dry storage. Demonstrate with an issued kit.
Pupils Teams / diagram sheets / labels / rulers Hardware kits / trays Waves Evidence sheets / pencils 10 4 4 1 10 15 5 5 1 15 20 7 7 1 20 25 9 5 2 25

Battery type/count and reserves follow the guide's setup card, not an assumed two-AA count. Reuse grids/parts and the same sheets in meeting 2.

docs.title: Vocabulary, background and safety
docs.text:
Circuit: conducting path including a return to the source. Open/closed: interrupted/complete path. Input/output: switch action/light response. Criterion: tested success requirement. Constraint: a limit. A battery supplies energy; current is charge flow, not energy "used up" by light.

Misconception: any arrangement of snapped parts is safe. If asked: "Why won't it light?" Isolate power; compare with the approved diagram and ask the teacher to check contacts/cells. Never bypass protection.

SAFETY: adult isolates the source before any snap change and checks before reconnecting. No pupil battery access, loose coin cells, household power, shorts, extra loads, live faults, fan blades, soldering or take-home hardware. Warm/smelly/leaking/damaged -> stop, tell adult, OUT OF SERVICE. Follow the guide, including the protected-AA or paper alternative when gated.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Purpose. Prayer: "God, help us use our gifts with care and include one another." Explain the real-turn rule and distinguish human dignity from circuit success.
  2. 4-8: Model. Teacher traces the approved full path, demonstrates OFF/ON, isolation and adult inspection. Do not distribute unused parts.
  3. 8-10: Predict. Each child draws the return path and predicts OFF/ON outputs.
  4. 10-22: Wave A. Teams follow the guide's isolated build, inspection, individual two-cycle switch tests and one teacher-managed open-path repair/retest. Waiting teams label diagrams and plan an ON/OFF label using words and symbols, not color alone.
  5. 22-23: Reset. Adult isolates power and transfers/resets station kits.
  6. 23-35: Wave B / feedback. Remaining teams receive the same hardware routine. Finished teams explain their repair and peer-check labels; at smaller enrollment, use this time for retests and individual checks. Ask each child: "Where is the gap? What evidence showed the repair worked?"
  7. 35-40: Cleanup. Isolate power, count/return parts and cells, store kits and save sheets/labels. Record physical evidence not yet collected.

docs.title: Meeting 2: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Retrieve. Review each child's diagram; model correct OFF/ON behavior again without assuming meeting 1 mastery.
  2. 4-8: Define. User brief: "A classmate needs to tell when this classroom model is ON or OFF." Criteria: two correct OFF/ON cycles and a peer can read the label from 1 m. Constraints: supplied grid, original approved circuit, no extra electrical parts.
  3. 8-10: Plan. Each child predicts one readability obstacle and proposes a label change.
  4. 10-22: Wave A. Rebuild/check/test using the guide. Test label at 1 m, record pass/not yet, revise one visual feature and retest. Change paper layout only, not the approved circuit.
  5. 22-23: Reset. Adult isolates power and transfers station kits.
  6. 23-35: Wave B / evidence. Remaining teams run the same routine. Finished teams record before/after results. Each child explains one criterion, constraint, observed revision and inclusion choice; not a medical/emergency device.
  7. 35-40: Cleanup. Isolate/count/store and collect individual evidence; paper labels only go home.

docs.title: Success, support and trouble
docs.text:
Every child contributes to the isolated team build, operates the switch, records two cycles, explains the full path/repair and cites a before/after label test. Team success alone does not certify each child's operation. Score 1 participation only; 2 path/test with prompts; 3 independent path/state explanation and test-backed revision; 4 additionally explains a design limitation and justifies an access tradeoff.

  • Grade 3/support: traced diagram, large labels, oral/dictated records and motor assistance. Every child still predicts and operates with support.
  • Grade 4/challenge: compare two possible open-path faults on paper; justify a word/symbol choice. No live shorts or undocumented extra branches.
  • 25 pupils: nine teams, five stations, two 12-minute waves; no four-pupil team. Inspection or access overruns mean deferred evidence, not rushed approval.
  • Missing/failed kit: isolate/report and use a checked reserve. Otherwise use paper and schedule the missing physical turn.

docs.title: Alternatives and family snippet
docs.text:
Use the guide's separate protected-AA switched-light route if verified. Without safe hardware, keep the same times with paper paths and an on/off token; record circuit reasoning/design evidence only; electrical operation not observed. All work is indoors; no homework or family purchases.

We traced and tested a switched light, then improved a classroom label using peer feedback. We practiced including others and caring for shared tools. Ask: "What did your test show, and what did you change?" Describe the actual hardware or paper route; no electrical project goes home.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Mathematics; one 40-minute meeting. Objective: measure two circles, compare around with three across-lengths and explain a remainder/measurement limit. Why/big idea: repeatable relationships support mathematical reasoning. Catholic/CST-C1: truthful approximation versus faith wonder; CST-M1: around/across measurements; CST-M3: three equal lengths plus remainder. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; developing, no required ratios/calculators/decimal division. Prep 10; cleanup 5 included.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Teams <=3 (⅘/7/9). Kit: two smooth plastic lids/plates of different sizes, ruler, four 50 cm string pieces. Per pupil: paper/pencil. Teacher board/timer; demo uses issued kit, ensure string reaches around both circles; select circles under 15 cm diameter. Write table circle | across cm | around cm | three across compared with around. Tools/string reusable; paper saved.

Allocation 10 15 20 25 Rulers (1/team) 4 5 7 9 Circles (2/team) 8 10 14 18 String pieces (4/team) 16 20 28 36 Paper; pencils (1/pupil each) 10 15 20 25

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: Diameter = across through center; circumference = around; approximation = close measurement. Pi is finite, between 3 and 4; its decimal expansion does not terminate/repeat periodically. Misconception: endless digits mean infinite size. If asked "Did we prove exact pi?" No; string/ruler readings approximate an ideal circle relationship. Faith wonder is not proof of theology. No sharp can lids, neck loops, compasses, treats or robot-circle commands. Desk string only; stop/report sharp edges. Indoor primary.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: "Is around closer to one, two or three across-lengths?" Predict; optional prayer of wonder without treating pi as God's measurement.
  2. 4-10: Model across through center, wrap string without stretching, then measure whole cm from zero.
  3. 10-22: Rotate measuring/recording; each pupil measures at least one around/across pair; team records both circles.
  4. 22-30: Lay three equal diameter-length portions along circumference; mark small remaining length. Remeasure one suspicious reading.
  5. 30-35: Each child records two pairs, demonstrates three diameters plus remainder and states approximation versus finite pi. "What could create error?"
  6. 35-40: Count/coil short strings, stack circles/rulers, collect dated table.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: two measurement pairs with units, three-length comparison and honest limit. Grade 3/support: teacher center mark, premarked equal portions, oral comparison. Grade 4/challenge: compare repeat readings and explain error, no required division. Around shorter than three across: check center/stretch/zero, record corrected measurement without hiding original. Missing circles: trace two teacher-selected circular bases, same task; do not use arbitrary oval. Early finish: explain why same relation does not mean same circumference.

Family: We compared around/across and learned pi is finite. Ask, "What was left after three across-lengths?" Optional: notice a circle, no measurement task.

docs.title: Lesson at a glance
docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Stewardship; three 40-minute meetings. Objective: observe clean sample materials, make a sorting system, compare two ten-card tests and distinguish modeled from actual waste reduction. Why: creation care needs usable routines and honest data. Catholic/CST-C3: reduce/reuse choice; CST-S1: observations; CST-E1: sorting criterion/limits; CST-E2: retest; CST-M2: two labeled results. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; developing. Prep 15; cleanup 5 each. Creation-care teaching paraphrases Laudato Si' opening; no inherited quotation or measured-savings claim.

docs.title: Before class and exact supplies
docs.text:
Teams <=3 (⅘/7/9). Per team/unit: two cardstock sign sheets, ten teacher-drawn large scenario cards (five clean unused paper, five clean reusable containers), two markers, tray, 40 cm tape. Cards are classroom practice categories, not municipal recycling rules. Per pupil: three evidence sheets/pencil. Teacher board/timer; draw card key, demo from issued set. No trash/waste handling or unattended building audit. Cards/tools reusable; signs/tape consumable.

docs.title: Vocabulary/background/SAFETY
docs.text: Reduce = use less; reuse = use again; recycling = material processing under local rules; impact = measured effect. Misconception: correct model sorting proves less landfill waste. If asked "Can this go in our real bin?" Ask the school's responsible adult/local rule, not this practice card. Dry cards only; no compost, sockets, plumbing, real pollutants, stagnant water or claims about family waste. Stop/report damaged supplies. Indoor primary.

docs.title: Meeting 1: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: "How can we care for shared resources without guessing results?"
  2. 4-10: Model observation versus inference on a clean paper/card sample.
  3. 10-22: Each sorts/notices card features, records two observations and labels a personal reduce/reuse option without disclosing home circumstances.
  4. 22-30: Baseline ten-card sort with neighboring peer, no coaching; tally correct placements using key. Identify confusing categories.
  5. 30-35: Individual baseline count, observation and possible criterion: at least eight correct of ten in two minutes.
  6. 35-40: Count cards/tools, save records, clear.

docs.title: Meeting 2: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: Retrieve baseline; choose confusion to address.
  2. 4-9: State limits two signs/40 cm tape; keep ten cards and two-minute test.
  3. 9-21: Build word/symbol sorting signs, every pupil authors one feature.
  4. 21-30: Neighbor tests ten cards, record count; revise one confusing feature and repeat identical-length test with shuffled cards.
  5. 30-35: Each records before/after, criterion and change rationale.
  6. 35-40: Count/save signs/cards; no real bin installation.

docs.title: Meeting 3: exactly 40 minutes
docs.text:
1. 0-4: "What result would justify recommending the routine?"
  2. 4-9: Model a two-bar chart 0-10, title and labels.
  3. 9-21: Run final ten-card test with new neighbor; individual bar chart compares baseline/final counts, not fabricated percentages.
  4. 21-30: Parallel peer explanation: evidence, reuse choice, model limit; revise recommendation for audience.
  5. 30-35: Each explains two bars and what adult observation would be needed to measure actual waste reduction.
  6. 35-40: Archive dated data, count/save kit, remove tape.

docs.title: Success/access/troubleshooting
docs.text:
Meets: observations, criterion/limit, actual repeated counts and chart/impact distinction. Grade 3/support: 0-10 template/oral evidence. Grade 4/challenge: compare changes and explain new-user sampling. Wrong sort: note confusion, revise sign, not key mid-test. No physical cards: draw ten on scrap paper; do not handle trash. Early finish: test different card order under same conditions.

Family: We tested a creation-care sorting model. Ask, "What did the data measure, and what didn't it measure?" Optional: discuss one reuse habit.

docs.text: Grades 3-4; Weekly A; Life science; one 40-minute meeting. Objective: observe a seed, order four living butterfly stages and explain why development is not biological Resurrection. Why: accurate biology and religious symbolism can coexist without confusing evidence. CST-C1 observation/faith distinction; CST-S1 seed detail; CST-S3 living stages/ generation link; CST-A1 labeled diagram. Official alignment VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Technology None; introductory. Teacher board/timer; allergy/handling check; demo uses issued set. No invented timing, live specimens, planting or hidden caretaker.
