All named audit terms resolve with explicit physical/resource/component/holding classification; no actual stock or classroom-use count was fabricated. The eight-kit holding remains separate and uninspected. The complete references' 10/15/20/25 quantity tables remain the exact issue lists; catalogue quantities are conservative planning stock, not simultaneous or cumulative annual demand.

docs.title: K-6 Catholic C-STREAM philosophy
docs.text: Local program philosophy. Planning date: 2026-10-04. School year: 2026-27. Not an MDE- or Archdiocese-approved curriculum.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
C-STREAM joins Catholic identity and faith with science, technology, engineering, art and mathematics. Students study creation carefully, ask honest questions, make and improve things, reason with quantities, communicate creatively and consider the dignity of people affected by their choices. Their growing skills can serve God, neighbor and the common good in everyday life and many vocations, not only future technical careers.

Catholic identity is more than an opening prayer. It shapes truthful reporting, stewardship, respectful collaboration, ethical technology use, purposeful work and service. Faith and reason strengthen inquiry rather than competing with it. Use an authentic connection when it deepens learning; do not attach a forced theological metaphor to every fact. Distinguish Church teaching, devotional tradition, an educator's analogy and scientific evidence. See the verified teaching and guidance in Standards Sources.

docs.title: Classroom commitments
docs.text:
• Hands-on first; technology for a reason. Begin with observation, objects, sketches, paper algorithms, cardboard models, rulers and reusable materials. Use devices when they materially enable programming, research, measurement, accessibility or another objective. Device consumption is not computer science. State None / Optional / Recommended / Required, explain Required, and provide a valid low-tech fallback where possible. Never claim the fallback proves a digital operation it does not perform.
  • Real disciplinary learning. Science asks for evidence; engineering tests solutions against needs and limits; mathematics supports reasoning; art involves intentional observation, form, meaning, critique and revision, not just decorating a finished product. Lessons need not give equal time to every domain, but the year should intentionally revisit all six local domains.
  • Failure is information. A weak prototype or unexpected result is a reason to investigate, not a judgment on the student. Reward evidence-based revision, intellectual honesty and thoughtful choices rather than winning or polish.
  • Safe and inclusive by design. Use school-approved materials and age-appropriate tools; make adult-only actions explicit. Avoid unknown substances, unsafe projectiles, mains electricity, loose button batteries and strong small magnets. Address allergies, choking hazards, water, sharp/hot tools and outdoor exposure. Use fictional or anonymous data rather than sensitive student/family information. Do not use classmates as experimental subjects for risky activities.
  • Every child can show learning. Model short oral/picture directions for K-1. Offer pointing, building, acting, drawing, oral explanation, scribing and assistive tools. Preserve the target while reducing irrelevant reading, writing, sensory or motor demands. Rotate roles; do not let a confident partner supply all the reasoning. Challenge adds depth, not compulsory expense.
  • Practical, reusable and weather-resilient. Prefer low-cost multipurpose kits and light preparation. Plan for 10, 15, 20 or 25 students with explicit quantities, team roles and cleanup. Outdoor learning has an indoor alternative; January cold, limited daylight or a cancelled outing must not erase an essential target.
  • No routine homework. Teach and assess core learning at school. Family conversations or observations are optional, ungraded invitations with an in-class equivalent. Participation never depends on home devices, purchases, donations, transport or an adult teaching the lesson.

docs.title: Fit the school's periods
docs.text:
These are example single-period budgets, including safety, setup and cleanup. Adjust for the actual activity; do not squeeze a full investigation into a shorter period by removing evidence or safety. Use a second meeting when needed.

Period Hook, objective, safety and demonstration Explore/build/test, including setup Individual check and explanation Cleanup 25 minutes 4 13 4 4 30 minutes 5 16 5 4 40 minutes 6 23 6 5 45 minutes 7 26 7 5

In short periods, use one meaningful test or design choice. In longer periods, add repeated testing or revision, not filler. Some processes need several meetings; store labelled work and resume rather than assigning completion at home.

docs.title: Evidence, continuity and honest claims
docs.text:
The eighteen local standards and seven-grade progression survive lesson changes. Combined-grade classes share a context but use separate grade-level success criteria. Weekly/bi-weekly schedules and A/B rotations need their own checked opportunities to learn and demonstrate those targets.

Keep assessment light but real: observation, an individual explanation, a sketch, a tested model or a data record. Participation and attractive group products are not mastery. Apply the individual evidence rule at planned checkpoints, and record what still needs teaching or assessment. Evaluate understanding of taught Catholic ideas and ethical choices, never private belief, perceived holiness or family religious practice.

External standards claims require a verified edition, grade/benchmark, matching lesson task and individual assessment. These local competencies do not certify full science, mathematics, arts, ELA, social studies, CS or religion coverage. The program complements primary subjects and OMCE guidance; local school/diocesan review remains necessary.

Teacher design test: Can a capable teacher or substitute explain the purpose, prepare the kit, teach safely, include every learner, finish cleanup and identify each child's learning within the available period? If not, simplify the activity, improve its supports or allow another meeting without weakening the target.

docs.title: Repository inventory and audit method
docs.text:
Baseline inspected: October 4, 2026. Planning year: 2026-27.

This inventory records the existing organization before curriculum changes. The review preserves the weekly/bi-weekly options, combined-grade rotations, existing URLs, and the school's 25/30/40/45-minute periods.

docs.title: Curriculum assets
docs.text:
The documentation tree contains 307 Markdown documents, including 251 lesson documents and supporting resources. A document is not necessarily a single class meeting: weekly filenames sometimes cover several weeks.

Grade band Weekly A or single track Weekly B Bi-weekly A or single track Bi-weekly B Kindergarten 20 Not applicable 17 Not applicable Grades 1-2 20 20 17 17 Grades 3-4 20 17 17 17 Grades 5-6 20 15 17 17 Total 80 52 68 51

The labels "34 lessons" and "17 sessions" in existing overview pages must not be used as file counts or evidence that every planned instructional week is covered. Holiday weeks and multi-week units require a separate pacing check.

Asset Existing location Function and review concern Weekly lessons docs/Lessons/ grade-band directories Activities, objectives, Catholic connections, procedures and assessments; quality must be checked individually. Bi-weekly lessons docs/Lessons/Bi-Weekly/ Separate condensed sequences, not extra lessons to add to the weekly year. Planning Year planner and lesson index Calendar and navigation; nominal lesson totals and actual meetings need reconciliation. Teacher resources docs/Resources/ Substitute, differentiation, equipment, family, volunteer and liturgical guides. Student resources docs/Student_Resources/ Journals, goals, reflection and engineering-process sheets; oral/drawn alternatives matter for emerging readers. Templates docs/Templates/ Lesson, project and cross-curricular unit formats; inconsistent arts terminology and digital-first assumptions need correction. Assessment docs/Rubrics/ Faith/reason, service, project and collaboration rubrics; distinguish participation from demonstrated learning. Publishing mkdocs.yml, overrides and stylesheets MkDocs Material site, print compilation and GitHub Pages workflow. Generated output site/, .cache/ Not authoritative curriculum; do not edit generated pages to change lessons.

There are no tracked curriculum-generation scripts, automated curriculum tests, structured lesson database, or standards/materials CSVs in the baseline. The existing dependency manifest supports documentation publication.

docs.title: Initial evidence, not conclusions about every lesson
docs.text:
• A Kindergarten robotics unit requires charged, paired robots and iPads. Direction, prediction and sequencing can also be taught physically; actual robot-operation objectives must remain distinct from an unplugged fallback.
  • A Grades 1-2 bridge session labels a papal bridge metaphor as Scripture. That attribution is inaccurate and needs correction, not repetition.
  • A Grades 3-4 bridge lesson includes efficiency ratios without establishing whether those calculations fit the younger grade's prerequisites.
  • A Grades 5-6 forensic session leaves sample preparation, "safe" unknown substances and fictional evidence unspecified. A substitute needs a complete, non-accusatory investigation with no unknown powders or real student profiling.
  • The general substitute guide asks for a quick-reference card without proving that such a card exists for every activity.
  • Home, planning and template pages emphasize digital art. Art also needs purposeful observational drawing, model design, pattern, composition and communication without a device.
  • Materials guidance mixes classroom basics with specialty robots, loan kits and apps. Availability, quantities, annual consumables and minimum operating cost must be separated.

docs.title: Audit method and change policy
docs.text:
Four grade-band workstreams inspect every lesson, record baseline findings, and make targeted improvements before publishing their audit. A separate standards workstream verifies authoritative sources. Program integration uses these records rather than inferring alignment from lesson titles or tags.

The internal mapping is grade -> rotation/schedule -> unit -> lesson -> demonstrated skills/local standards -> materials -> assessment. Evidence records distinguish original quality from the revision state.

Audit dispositions are KEEP, KEEP + IMPROVE, REBUILD, REPLACE and REMOVE. No file is deleted merely because an alternative is preferred. Recommendations retain useful activities and identify safety, accuracy and substitute-readiness issues first.

Quality uses four evidence levels: 0 absent/unsafe, 1 named but underspecified, 2 teachable with a specific support or remaining check, 3 explicit and independently usable. Dimensions include academic rigor, developmental fit, Catholic integration, standards evidence, hands-on engagement, instruction/substitute clarity, low-tech access, cost/preparation, assessment, inclusion, safety, scalability, family communication and progression. Scores are editorial judgments, not classroom-outcome measurements.

Verification limits: A document review cannot certify actual school inventory, individual accommodations, equipment condition, classroom outcomes, diocesan approval or complete coverage of the primary subject curricula. Unverified official benchmarks are marked VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

docs.title: School release checklist
docs.text: Repository completion means a complete written pathway, traceable planned evidence and passing document checks. It does not establish physical kit condition, the school's permissions, individual access needs or actual learning. These are concrete checks the school can complete, not more curriculum reports to commission.

docs.title: Before the selected lesson
docs.text:
Check Responsible role to assign Record before release Calendar and objective Grade teacher One schedule/rotation; actual date, native period, core objective and chosen physical/device/paper pathway. Counted kit Teacher/materials coordinator Actual location, issue/return quantities for the enrolled class, missing/damaged items and teacher-only tools. A catalogue name or report is not a count. Safe materials School safety lead/teacher Condition, allergies, ingredients, age guidance, water/hygiene, tool restrictions and activity-specific stop rules. Electrical pretest, if used Qualified school adult Matching model/manual/project, safe supply/covers/protection, correct approved diagram and successful inspection/test. No invented Snap component or battery allocation. Device/access pretest, if used School technology lead Approved actual host/app/version, privacy/account/accessibility settings, executable test and working turn plan. Individual access Teacher/support staff Reading, motor, sensory, language and physical accommodations preserving the target; consent for physical assistance. Prepared content Teacher Exact source/model-data/picture content, no unverified biography/quotation and no personal student data in fictional scenarios. Handoff Teacher/substitute Kit and lesson together, actual school contact, objective check, cleanup and fallback. First-use kit construction/charging/freezing happens beforehand.

If an essential condition fails, hold that pathway. Use only the named alternative, state its changed objective and record deferred evidence. Paper reasoning cannot release actual software execution, robot operation, circuit construction, live observations or measured weather.

docs.title: Pilot evidence: collect, do not assume
docs.text:
Pilot at least one younger-grade and one older-grade complete reference, then the next scheduled unit. Record:

  1. Actual first/repeat preparation and in-class transition/cleanup minutes.
  2. Correct material allocation and actual consumption/returns.
  3. Each child's objective-linked demonstration and support used.
  4. Whether every child received a meaningful choice/tool/test turn.
  5. Unexpected safety, accessibility, space or timing constraints.
  6. The one change needed before the next use.

Compare the written threshold with the actual result: for example, a structure held ten seconds unaided, a two-command route was correctly predicted and debugged, or a child explained a recorded change using evidence. Do not replace a missing result with participation, photographs or a certificate. Use two dated individual observations where the local progression specifies an expected-mastery checkpoint.

docs.title: Source and institutional review
docs.text:
• Confirm the school's 2026-27 mathematics baseline/transition decision.
  • Obtain school-issued OMCE religion/culture policies and applicable curriculum expectations through authorized school channels.
  • Obtain inaccessible final MDE benchmark tables before restoring exact science/mathematics/ELA/social-studies claims.
  • Corroborate state-agency arts copies against the MDE official edition for a formal institutional alignment claim.
  • Treat CSTA 2026 as a verified national framework, not automatically adopted Minnesota or Archdiocesan standards.
  • Use only the precise task/evidence scope of an external-candidate mapping. A source-verified identifier is not proof the pupil mastered it.

The local C-STREAM competencies can guide teaching while these formal external claims remain withheld. They complement, not replace, primary subject curricula.

docs.title: Reported eight Snap Circuits kits
docs.text: The holding reports eight individual OHM-135 kits. Record actual manufacturer model, matching instructions, completeness, condition and age/power approval for each SC01-SC08. The classroom guide gives the bounded wave plan and evidence checks. An out-of-service kit is not a station; one wave cannot serve 25 pupils in eight groups of at most three. K remains optional adult-demonstration only.

docs.title: Release record to copy
docs.text:
Lesson / schedule / rotation:
Date / enrollment / native minutes:
Selected pathway / objective / individual evidence threshold:
Actual kit location / checker / check date:
Required items and teacher tools counted:
Safety, access and policy checks completed:
Pretest result and named fallback:
Objectives/evidence deferred if the pathway changes:
Pilot timing, individual evidence and next revision:
Teacher / school approver where required:

Do not mark a blank release record approved. Record real school checks and revise the relevant lesson/kit after a failure. No commit, deployment, generic document score or schema pass substitutes for this evidence.

docs.title: Choose a feasible year
docs.text:
Retain the existing periods: K 25 minutes, Grades 1-2 30 minutes, Grades 3-4 40 minutes, Grades 5-6 45 minutes.

  • Bi-weekly: Select one existing 17-session track.
  • Weekly: Select one band/rotation. The common Year A scaffold covers 34 calendar slots, including two breaks, for 32 teaching meetings. Check Year B against its grade review; fewer documents can cover longer units and do not prove identical pacing.
  • Do not combine weekly and bi-weekly tracks or add all thematic menu entries to the selected year.
  • Core: Preserve inquiry, measurement/data, purposeful art, design/test/ redesign, unplugged computing and Catholic ethical reflection.
  • Recommended: Additional investigations or retesting that deepen an existing objective.
  • Optional/enrichment: Specialty robotics, advanced software, elaborate exhibitions, field trips and extra build variants when they add learning.

The legacy index's single-week/multi-week/long-arc quotas double-counted meetings. The corrected planner and downloadable audits replace that arithmetic. No grade should be scheduled simply by counting filenames.

Band 17 meetings: contact minutes 32 meetings: contact minutes K 425 800 1-2 510 960 3-4 680 1,280 5-6 765 1,440

These totals include distribution, transitions, assessment and cleanup. The weekly program has more practice time; equal mastery in half the time is not assumed.

The audited weekly Year B tracks for Grades 3-4 and 5-6 represent 33 meetings, or 1,320 and 1,485 minutes, respectively. Their units include the nominal winter-break slot; reconcile this with the actual school calendar rather than treating it as an extra guaranteed teaching meeting.

docs.title: Program unit spine
docs.text:
This is a local planning organization of recurring concepts, not a claim that every legacy lesson already has this title or alignment. The actual lesson-level unit, rotation, evidence and disposition are in the lesson map. Use the band reviews to select ready lessons and adapt themes to the real school/liturgical calendar.

Unit and bi-weekly slots Concepts and competencies Principal local standards Main evidence/project Weekly depth 1. Wonder, observation and tools; 1-2 Notice, ask, predict; tools carry out human purposes; truthful observation CST-C1, CST-S1, CST-T1, CST-M1 Oral/drawn observation; directional or tool demonstration Repeat observations and introduce team routines 2. Structures and forces; 3-4 Problem, criterion, constraints, stable forms, fair comparison CST-E1, CST-E2, CST-M1, CST-A1 Bridge/tower prototype, measured test and revision Compare alternatives and retest under the same load 3. Creation, patterns and community; 5-6 Living/physical systems as appropriate; purposeful pattern; service CST-S3, CST-C2, CST-A2, CST-M2 Model or useful design with an explanation of who benefits Observe/change one feature and collect individual explanations 4. Light, sound and sequences; 7-8 Physical systems, input/output, algorithms and visual/audio communication CST-S3, CST-T2, CST-A3 Light/sound model or paper algorithm with a trace Safe circuit investigation or actual digital execution when justified 5. Evidence, faith/reason and local conditions; 9-10 Honest evidence, biography/source checks, weather/measurement/data CST-C1, CST-S1, CST-S2, CST-M2 Investigation record with evidence and uncertainty Compare observations across time; revise an explanation 6. Life, stewardship and service; 11-13 Change over time, systems, resource care, inclusive design CST-C3, CST-S3, CST-E1, CST-C2 Indoor growth/habitat model or service prototype Repeated observations, testing and feedback 7. Systems, redesign and responsible technology; 14-16 Algorithms, mechanisms, criteria, tradeoffs and ethical impacts CST-T2, CST-T3, CST-E2, CST-E3 Debugged plan or tested mechanism with a justified improvement Evaluate alternate designs; digital/hardware extensions only when meaningful 8. Communicate and reflect; 17 Explain learning, compare earlier/later work, revise communication CST-A3, CST-E3, CST-C3 Individual explanation plus a team display/model Practice feedback, revise display and collect final evidence

Codes are local program competencies, not official benchmarks. Each individual lesson claims only what students actually practice and demonstrate. Not every unit needs every domain. Arts must include purposeful choices and communication; counting decoration as art or a tablet as computing is insufficient.

docs.title: Grade-specific progression and memorable experiences
docs.text:
Grade Entry/prerequisite to establish End-of-grade performance to seek Signature experience and next step K Follow one modeled oral instruction; compare visible objects Observe, build, point/draw/tell one change; count/compare a small set Structures that connect/help; next explain a problem and simple instruction sequence 1 Reestablish safe tool use, oral sequencing and counting Build for a purpose, trace a short sequence, describe a result Paper bridge; next explain choices and represent results 2 Repeat Grade 1 demonstrations rather than assume they were taught in the other rotation Explain design choice, compare measured results and revise an algorithm/design A service structure/mechanism with a before/after explanation; next conduct fair tests 3 Model criteria, test procedure, measurement units and a simple table Test a design under fixed conditions and use evidence to suggest a revision Measured bridge; next use repeated measures and clearer evidence 4 Recheck fair testing, recording and distinguishing prediction from result Use measurements and evidence to improve a design or explanation Structures, indoor weather inquiry or safe circuits; next compare against multiple criteria 5 Establish criteria/constraints, repeated observations and respectful feedback Compare designs using evidence, criteria, cost/resources and an ethical reason Service design or environmental model; next defend a tradeoff and identify limitations 6 Reestablish data quality, computational trace and explanation of users' needs Defend design choices with evidence, tradeoffs, cost, ethics and performance Inclusive design exhibition or fictional evidence investigation; next transfer methods to independent inquiry

These are desired local outcomes, not automatic promotions based on exposure. The learning progression gives competency-level introduced/developing/reinforced/expected indicators and individual evidence.

docs.title: Rotations and prerequisites
docs.text:
Year A and B are alternative entry years, not beginner/advanced levels. Every rotation must reintroduce the design cycle, safe tool routines, relevant vocabulary, measurement method and computing representations. Younger students receive modeling and accessible responses; older students extend evidence, independence and justification.

Repeat the skill intentionally, not an identical worksheet or unexamined product. Keep a small portfolio so a returning student can compare earlier and later reasoning. When a project recurs, increase only an appropriate dimension: independence, precision, data, number of criteria or ethical tradeoffs.

docs.title: Seasonal and workload controls
docs.text:
• No required objective depends on outdoor access in a Minnesota winter. Use room-temperature materials, safe indoor observations and prepared data when appropriate; do not claim a paper model supplies real weather data.
  • Growing investigations require observations over time. Schedule follow-up checks explicitly; a single period cannot demonstrate a life cycle.
  • Start with reusable kits and common classroom materials. Specialist kit reservations and digital accounts are VERIFICATION REQUIRED.
  • Keep projects small enough to test and assess in the native period. If a longer project is selected, label the meetings and storage/reset steps.
  • Use the audit's prep/cleanup estimates as planning estimates, not measured teacher timings. Time a first run and record improvements.
  • No routine homework. Family questions and activities are optional and do not supply evidence required for participation or mastery.

docs.title: Grade-band evidence
docs.text: Read the detailed K, 1-2, 3-4 and 5-6 reviews for exact track counts, original strengths/gaps, targeted revisions, remaining developmental concerns and unit newsletter snippets.

docs.title: Standards sources and implementation status
docs.text: Planning date and source access date: 2026-10-04. Target school year: 2026-27. All source entries record research on that date; the register distinguishes directly inspected text, indexed document references and failed retrievals. These are concise paraphrases, not reproductions of standards. Source years are edition labels; they are not necessarily adoption or implementation years.

docs.title: Classification and claim limits
docs.text:
• Official standard: Minnesota's adopted subject standards. Their public-school implementation dates are a reference for this Catholic school's planning, not a finding that every public-school accountability requirement applies here.
  • Official guidance/teaching: MDE implementation guidance; Archdiocesan guidance or policy; Vatican/USCCB teaching. These are not interchangeable with numbered academic benchmarks.
  • National standard/framework: CSTA, NGSS, National Core Arts Standards and ISTE. Use selectively; no Minnesota or Archdiocesan adoption is inferred.
  • Local program standard: The eighteen CST-* competencies in Local Standards. Not MDE-approved, not Archdiocese-approved, and not a complete subject curriculum.

Source verification does not establish lesson alignment. No external benchmark number is assigned to a lesson by this research. A claim requires the exact edition, applicable grade, verified benchmark, matching student task and assessment evidence. A topic resemblance or a local code is insufficient. All generated external-alignment fields remain VERIFICATION REQUIRED until that benchmark + lesson + individual assessment/evidence mapping is reviewed. A verified source, implementation date or local-code entry does not remove this hold.

docs.title: Minnesota: the 2026-27 baseline
docs.text:
The directly inspected MDE newsletters and enacted rules establish these dates. Older projected transition timelines must not override the later confirmations. Assessment rollout dates are not substitutes for instruction implementation dates. In particular, the October 2023 newsletter called the social studies and math dates anticipated; the enacted rules and April 2026 confirmation, not that earlier forecast alone, establish the transition years used below.

Area Use for 2026-27 Verified implementation status Grade scope and limits Evidence Science 2019 Minnesota Academic Standards in Science Full implementation occurred in 2024-25; already implemented in 2026-27. Official rule applies K-12. Use the actual benchmark for each K-6 grade, not a generic elementary topic. Direct inspection of the final grade/benchmark tables remains VERIFICATION REQUIRED. MN-01, MN-02 Mathematics 2007 Minnesota K-12 Academic Standards in Mathematics as the existing-edition planning baseline 2022 standards are adopted, but implementation begins 2027-28, not 2026-27. Clearly label any early use as transition/enrichment. Official new rule applies K-12. The MDE existing-edition PDF is identified below, but was not directly readable; confirm the school's 2007 benchmark selections and transition decision: VERIFICATION REQUIRED. MN-01, MN-03, MN-08 Arts 2018 Minnesota Academic Standards in Arts Education Full implementation 2023-24; ongoing in 2026-27. MDE's April 2026 notice says the next review is 2027-28, with a later implementation year to be set in rulemaking. A review is not a replacement standard. State-agency workbook directly shows individual grades K, 1-8, plus HS; K is encoded as grade 0. Do not reuse the older 2008 K-¾-5 band labels as the 2018 structure. Five arts areas; local visual design does not cover all five. MN-01, MN-04, MN-05 English language arts 2020 Minnesota K-12 Academic Standards in ELA Full implementation 2025-26; already implemented in 2026-27. Official rule applies K-12. Reading, writing, and listening/speaking/viewing/exchanging ideas support explanations and communication. Exact grade-table organization and K-6 benchmark selection remain VERIFICATION REQUIRED. MN-01, MN-06 Social studies 2021 Minnesota K-12 Academic Standards in Social Studies Effective at the beginning of 2026-27; this is its implementation year, not a future transition. Official rule applies K-12. Community needs, resources and technology impacts are possible connections, not proof of coverage. Final grade/benchmark selections remain VERIFICATION REQUIRED. MN-01, MN-07 Computer science integration Verify CS-bearing benchmarks within the applicable subject edition MDE confirms CS-integrated benchmarks in 2019 science; their subject implementation is 2024-25. The 2018 arts workbook identifies CS-related benchmarks. There is no separate CS implementation deadline verified by this research. Do not give every K-6 grade the same benchmark or treat device operation as CS. The full integrated K-12 collection, subject-specific grade rows and any additional current legal/framework deadlines are VERIFICATION REQUIRED. MN-01, MN-05, MN-09

docs.title: Minnesota source register
docs.text:
ID / classification Authoritative URL(s), accessed 2026-10-04 Inspected evidence and permitted use MN-01 / official implementation guidance MDE, April 28, 2026; MDE, October 2, 2023 Both newsletters were directly readable, including underlying HTML. The 2023 notice confirms arts 2023-24. The 2026 notice confirms science 2024-25, ELA 2025-26, social studies 2026-27 and mathematics 2027-28, and ongoing 2018 arts implementation. The final-document URL is linked by MN-01; portal/document retrieval encountered a browser-verification barrier. No unseen benchmark IDs are asserted. The 2026 newsletter confirms the 2022 edition. Portal/document grade tables were not directly accessible. Page and workbook directly inspected. Workbook grade column contains 0-8 and HS; key defines 0 as Kindergarten and marks CS-related benchmarks. It says the MDE-hosted Excel is the official version. The underlying CS documents encountered the browser barrier. Integration is verified in science and identified in the arts workbook; an all-subject crosswalk, its current revision and other implementation claims are VERIFICATION REQUIRED. A bill proposal or a predicted framework deadline is not evidence of an enacted requirement.

Access limitation: Search summaries sometimes mixed older and newer editions or proposed and final dates. They were used to locate primary documents, not as authority for a benchmark number. MDE's challenge pages did not constitute access to their underlying documents. Directly inspected Revisor rules and MDE newsletters resolve the implementation dates; unresolved grade-level details remain flagged.

docs.title: Archdiocese and OMCE
docs.text:
ID / classification Authoritative URL, accessed 2026-10-04 Concise finding and implementation status ARCH-01 / official office guidance Office for the Mission of Catholic Education Directly inspected page/HTML: OMCE provides vision, support and direction for teaching in the Church's name and forming disciples; Catholic schooling forms the whole student. It is not a numbered K-6 C-STREAM standards document. ARCH-02 / official Archdiocesan strategic guidance Educating children and young people for discipleship Directly inspected: connects faith throughout learning with the Roadmap for Excellence in Catholic Education and supports its implementation. This establishes the initiative, not a C-STREAM benchmark list. ARCH-03 / official Archdiocesan reporting of Roadmap guidance The Catholic Spirit: Roadmap work and OMCE changes The Archdiocese's newspaper reports the Roadmap launched in 2019, with work on governance, talent, curriculum/metrics, access/sustainability and mission schools. Historical strategic reporting; not a current subject-standard implementation mandate. ARCH-04 / official Archdiocesan reporting of current curriculum guidance The Catholic Spirit: integrated Catholic curriculum Directly inspected 2026 report attributes guidance to OMCE's curriculum specialist: religion/culture expectations released September 2025; schools expected to begin adopting recommended programs/curricula in 2026-27 and move toward full implementation over the following five years. Focus is elementary/middle school; K-8 leaders received training. This is reporting of guidance, not direct inspection of the full school-issued framework or a K-6 C-STREAM mandate. ARCH-05 / official policy and support entry points Policy Compendium; OMCE Mission Support Directly inspected: the compendium describes its policies as binding according to applicability; support page provides office resources. The full school-issued 2023 policy manual, integrated curriculum framework and sample five-year roadmap were not inspected. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for the school's applicable versions and obligations.

Bounded finding: Among the public office page, Roadmap references, official news reports, policy landing page and OMCE support listing inspected here, no detailed K-6 C-STREAM performance-standard/code catalog was located. This is not a claim that such standards do not exist. School-distributed, restricted, unindexed or subsequently published materials may exist. Ask the principal/OMCE for the current Integrated Catholic Curriculum for Religion and Culture, applicable school policies and any subject/C-STREAM standards before claiming Archdiocesan alignment or approval.

The four principles reported in ARCH-04 are academic achievement/integration, virtue formation/human development, spiritual life and apostolic discernment. They inform this program's philosophy; the eighteen local codes are not representations of an official OMCE code set.

docs.title: Catholic teaching: verified paragraph references
docs.text:
All paragraphs below were seen on the official Vatican site, including page HTML where the simplified reader omitted body text. Classroom applications are local interpretations of teaching, not official academic standards.

ID / classification Official URL and exact references, accessed 2026-10-04 Paraphrase / classroom application FAITH-01 / official Church teaching CCC: characteristics of faith, 159 Faith and reason are not rival sources of truth; legitimate scientific investigation need not contradict faith. Keep observations and explanations honest; do not use theology as an experimental result. FAITH-02 / official Church teaching CCC: the human person as God's image, 1702, 1704 Every person bears God's image; reason participates in understanding creation and seeking the good. Design for people's dignity and access, not their productivity or presumed ability. FAITH-03 / official Church teaching CCC: respect for personal dignity, 2293-2295 Science and technology serve human flourishing and are not morally neutral merely because they are efficient. Human experimentation has moral and consent limits. Classroom implication: safe models, privacy, no harmful experiments on classmates. FAITH-04 / official Church teaching CCC: persons and goods, 2415-2418 Respect creation and its resources, consider future generations, and avoid needless animal suffering. Reuse materials, minimize waste and observe living things responsibly. FAITH-05 / official Church teaching CCC: work and social justice, 2427-2428 Work proceeds from persons and can develop their gifts; people are not instruments of production. Value careful making, every honest vocation and service rather than speed or prestige. FAITH-06 / official Church teaching CCC: living in truth, 2468-2469 Truthfulness in actions and words sustains trust. Record actual results, acknowledge uncertainty and credit another person's idea.

USCCB inspection limit: The seven themes of Catholic social teaching and care for creation were attempted on 2026-10-04 but reliable text retrieval was blocked or incomplete. Their detailed wording and any proposed USCCB-specific citation are VERIFICATION REQUIRED. The applications above rest on the directly inspected Vatican paragraphs, not on unverified USCCB text.

docs.title: Optional national resources
docs.text:
ID / classification Authoritative URL(s), accessed 2026-10-04 Verified status, grade organization and permitted use NAT-01 / national CS standards CSTA 2026 PK-12 standards; published standards view; publisher's current 2026 PDF download; development history; current publication statement on the 2017 archive page 2026 edition is published, not merely a revision in progress. The currently retrieved archive page explicitly says publication was July 2026. The active viewer and actual PDF download independently establish a released edition, rather than a planned release inferred from an old announcement. Direct HTML inspection verifies PK/K combined, individual grades 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, middle school 6-8, high school 9-12. Grade 6 belongs to the middle-school band, not to a single-grade Grade 6 standard. Concepts include algorithms/design, programming, data/analysis, systems/security and computing/society. No local adoption date or complete CSTA alignment is asserted. NAT-02 / historical national CS standards CSTA 2017 interactive archive; original 2017 workbook Retain only explicitly 2017-labelled legacy mappings. Workbook directly verifies K-2, 3-5, 6-8 and 9-10 band labels; these must not be copied into the 2026 elementary structure. An inconsistent middle-level band label on the interactive page was resolved using the original workbook. No 2017 benchmark number is assigned to a lesson here. NAT-03 / national science/engineering framework and standards NGSS three-dimensional learning; NGSS topic arrangements Directly inspected: practices, crosscutting concepts and disciplinary core ideas work together; investigation asks explanatory questions, while engineering addresses design problems. Optional planning guidance, not an assertion that Minnesota adopted every NGSS performance expectation. Exact grade-band PE mapping is VERIFICATION REQUIRED before use. NAT-04 / national arts standards National Core Arts Standards Directly inspected page/HTML: creating, performing/presenting/producing, responding and connecting; includes visual arts and other arts. Optional guidance. Use MN-05 for Minnesota's edition and grade structure. No unseen national arts code or one-to-one equivalence is claimed. NAT-05 / national technology standards ISTE Standards for Students Directly inspected page/HTML: digital citizenship, research, design, computational thinking and communication are useful lenses. The site describes ongoing updates. Not Minnesota subject standards and not proof of CS programming proficiency; exact indicator/version mappings are VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

CSTA's pages describe attribution/noncommercial/share-alike licensing. This framework uses original local performance descriptions, not a reproduced or renumbered CSTA standards set. Check permissions before redistributing external standards text or publishing a derivative crosswalk.

Current-release check, 2026-10-04: The publisher's 2026 download returned HTTP 200, application/pdf, and a valid PDF header, resolving to its July 2026 hosted document. The live viewer offered the grade choices recorded in NAT-01. An older notice that a revision was scheduled for 2026 would not, by itself, support a claim of publication. The publication month here comes from the publisher's explicit past-tense statement, not just a URL date or the planning date.

docs.title: Legacy public-page claims: verification and safe wording
docs.text:
This ledger supports qualification of shared home/README pages and related resources. It does not approve their legacy attributions or change external lesson-alignment fields. The local eighteen-code framework and twelve design principles are not an NCEA standards set, an empirically validated intervention or a Cognia certification.

ID / classification Claim and primary-source status, researched 2026-10-04 Verification requirement and usable qualification LEGACY-01 / national Catholic education guidance; exact attribution unverified NCEA's ten characteristics of STREAM schools and claims of meeting "NCEA standards." The directly inspected NCEA Talk, STREAM in Action: Easy to Find is a contributed practitioner article about faith, service and STREAM, not the exact ten-item publication or a review of this curriculum. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for the original NCEA title, author, edition/date, exact list and any claimed correspondence. Do not use secondary lists as proof of NCEA's precise wording or numbering. Safe wording: local STREAM reflection checklist. Neither the article nor a checklist establishes NCEA approval, accreditation or program-wide alignment. LEGACY-02 / local design principles; research-validation claim unverified "Research-backed"/"research-based" twelve success factors, effectiveness claims and claims of demonstrated student outcomes. No baseline study set, claim-by-claim evidence synthesis or evaluation of this curriculum was supplied or verified. NAT-03 verifies science/engineering framework guidance, not the effectiveness of all twelve local principles or these lessons. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for each empirical claim: identifiable original research, applicable age/context, supported finding and limits, plus evidence for any claimed local outcome. Safe wording: local design principles informed by selected guidance. Do not call the program research-validated, proven effective or certified because a source describes its own framework as research-based. LEGACY-03 / national organizational certification guidance; local award/status unverified Cognia STEM certification/accreditation or conformity claims. The directly inspected current Cognia STEM certification page describes third-party evaluation and distinguishes institutional accreditation from STEM certification. Its FAQ says accreditation is not required to pursue STEM certification and describes certification as a six-year term. These are Cognia's current process descriptions, not findings about this school or repository. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for the named institution/program's award, issuer, scope and current term; obtain Cognia-issued evidence or a verified official status record. Separate accreditation from STEM certification. Exact standards-edition conformity also needs a reviewed crosswalk and evidence. Safe wording: Cognia offers a separate STEM certification process; this curriculum makes no certification or accreditation claim. A school's accreditation does not by itself establish STEM certification, and curriculum guidance is not an award. LEGACY-04 / training/material attribution unverified Steno training materials, attributed inspirational quotations and other unattributed source wording in legacy public pages. No exact original publication, author/date or training document was inspected for these claims. VERIFICATION REQUIRED before attributing exact wording, describing the materials as research evidence or implying provider endorsement. Use clearly identified local paraphrases/design commitments until the original source and appropriate attribution are established.

The NCEA article and Cognia process page are primary evidence only for what those pages actually describe. They do not establish that a historical ten-characteristic list matches the local checklist, that a provider's research validates this curriculum, or that the school has earned any credential. Unverified claims should be qualified or omitted, not converted into assertions that the publication, research or credential does not exist.

docs.title: Scientific-heritage source cards completed
docs.text:
The updated heritage guide replaces unsourced quotations/priority claims with original, bounded cards:

Source Directly inspected facts and limits Masaryk University Mendel Museum Augustinian membership/abbacy, pea experiments and original collection/work; not a personal-faith quotation or classroom inheritance protocol. Pontifical Academy of Sciences, Lemaitre Institutional priest/cosmology/university-role record and 1894-1966 dates; no unsupported sole-discovery or papal-conversation claim. Benedict XVI, Albert, March 24, 2010 Dominican/natural-discipline history and observation/classification method, explicitly distinct from later scientific methods. University of St Andrews, Agnesi Scholarly secondary history of a mathematical teaching text and Catholic charitable work; not primary personal testimony or a simplistic first-professor claim.

All were inspected October 4, 2026 and paraphrased. Blocked Observatory retrievals/search summaries were not used to upgrade unseen biographical claims. The classroom applications assess actual inquiry/communication, not biography recall as science mastery.

Completion-pass source checks, October 4: normal MDE PDF, Excel (PROD059198) and annotated-document requests still returned browser verification HTML rather than readable benchmark tables; no challenge bypass or inferred identifier was used. The Perpich state-agency workbook's exact Grades 1-6 visual-arts creation/revision rows were inspected directly. The current CSTA publisher viewer's normal public index/detail request also returned exact 2026 identifiers and implementation boundaries, including grade-specific elementary codes and the Grade 6 middle-school band. Only task/evidence matches that meet the inspected scope are proposed; neither national publication nor a state-agency copy establishes local institutional approval or actual mastery.

Autonomous follow-up, October 4: the state-agency 2018 workbook was downloaded and its K visual-arts/music rows inspected directly. Twelve source-verified K candidates use four exact identifiers, actual rewritten tasks and scoped individual evidence. The workbook's MDE-official-copy note and institutional review hold are retained. Normal math/science retrieval and integrated-browser reading did not provide readable final tables; the repealed 3501.0710 page and missing 3501.0970 page were not substituted for unseen current identifiers.

  1. Obtain the current final MDE benchmark documents through normal authorized access. Inspect each proposed K, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 row, its edition, full requirement and any coding notes. Science, math, ELA and social studies exact grade-table organization was not directly verified here. Do not publish guessed external benchmark IDs or copy older grade bands into a newer edition.
  2. Confirm the school's primary math edition for 2026-27 and any intentional early transition to 2022; keep implemented and transition mappings separate.
  3. Inspect MDE's current integrated CS collection and supporting guidance. Confirm all proposed subject/grade mappings and any newly enacted requirements. The inspected evidence does not substantiate a standalone CS framework deadline, nor automatic Minnesota adoption of the July 2026 CSTA publication.
  4. Obtain OMCE's school-issued religion/culture framework, policy manual and implementation roadmap. Verify school-specific expectations and any detailed C-STREAM standards not found in the inspected public sources.
  5. For every lesson claim, record source/edition, exact verified benchmark, applicable grade/band, task, individual assessment, success criterion and evidence location. An unplugged substitute cannot satisfy a requirement to operate or program a computing device merely by covering similar concepts.
  6. Mark unsupported crosswalk rows VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Complete subject coverage, diocesan approval, actual student mastery and classroom outcomes cannot be certified by this source review or the eighteen-code framework.
  7. Retain the LEGACY-01 through LEGACY-04 qualifications on shared public pages and downstream templates. Obtain the original NCEA/training publications, empirical evidence and current institution-specific Cognia award records before restoring stronger attribution, research or certification claims.

See Local Standards, Learning Progression and Philosophy for the local planning and assessment contract.

docs.text:

docs.title: What a row means
docs.text:
Each traceability row connects a local program standard -> grade band -> schedule and rotation -> unit -> lesson -> planned assessment evidence. Filter the CSV by local_standard, grade_band, rotation and schedule. For example, filter CST-E2, 3-4, A, Weekly to find build/test/redesign opportunities and the evidence a teacher should collect.

The combined-grade row does not imply identical expectations for both grades. Use the grade-specific performance descriptions in the progression and the support/challenge guidance in the lesson. Students may enter either rotation; introduce required procedures and vocabulary before increasing independence.

The audit's status records the baseline disposition, while revision records subsequent changes. A lesson marked REBUILD and rebuilt has been revised; a baseline concern is not erased from the change record. improved is not a substitute-readiness certification. Read the band review and the actual lesson before scheduling.

These are editorial alignment judgments about intended student work. They are not evidence that a class has mastered a standard. A general exit check may support only part of a competency; teachers must collect the individual performance evidence specified in the local progression.

docs.title: Material queries
docs.text:
Filter the material-usage CSV by grade_band, schedule and rotation to see what the selected lessons name. item_id connects an exact canonical/alias name to the normalized inventory. This is text matching only, not verified reference_kind separates physical inventory from executable-platform access, teacher-prepared documentation and reported holdings. RESOURCE:* and STOCK:* references have no invented purchase price or verified ownership. Local access and hardware preflight remain explicit. A manufacturer manual is not the circuit kit, and a paper portfolio is not observed student mastery. This is text matching only, not verified item specifications, quantity sufficiency, ownership or safety. Unmatched and ambiguous terms are retained visibly for reconciliation rather than assigned an invented substitute. The inventory's verified-use count remains separate from these textual occurrences.

The reconciliation queue groups remaining occurrences by exact term, grade and source lesson, with an explicit follow-up reason. A suggested triage category is not a supplier/item equivalence: software/access, record formats, quantity phrases, ambiguous adhesives and safety-critical parts still need their actual lesson specifications. It is a work queue, not a purchase list.

docs.title: Official standards claim gate
docs.text:
Every generated external-alignment field is VERIFICATION REQUIRED. This is intentional, not a substitute for the source research. An official claim needs all of the following:

  1. Applicable adopted/implemented version and school year.
  2. Verified exact benchmark identifier, grade and source URL/document.
  3. Student action that actually practices the benchmark.
  4. Specific assessment evidence for the relevant part of the benchmark.
  5. Reviewer/date and any scope limitations.

A topic resemblance, Catholic quotation, tag, device, or project photograph does not establish official alignment. This enrichment program does not replace the school's science, mathematics, arts, ELA, social studies or religion curricula.

The separate exact external matrix now contains 29 source-specific candidates using sixteen identifiers. Its verified source scope and school/MDE-copy/national-framework boundaries are explicit. The general local-map field does not silently upgrade every other standard claim to official alignment.

docs.title: Updating and validating
docs.text:
The four band-audit CSVs are the source of the combined maps. From the repository root in PowerShell:

.\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1
.\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1 -ValidateOnly
.\scripts\Test-CurriculumMaps.ps1
.\scripts\Test-LessonReferences.ps1
mkdocs build --strict

For the current K version-3.0 reference set, update lesson metadata and the individual-evidence definitions together, then run .\scripts\Sync-KindergartenAudit.ps1 and .\scripts\Test-KindergartenReferences.ps1 before regenerating the maps. The K validator checks 29 autonomous references/37 native meetings, class-size arithmetic and complete audit evidence; it does not approve physical kits or certify learning outcomes.

The script fails explicitly on missing or duplicate lessons, invalid schema/enums, schedule/rotation mismatches, wrong period lengths, missing evidence fields and unknown local standard codes. It also verifies that every lesson file appears exactly once and all 18 codes exist in the catalog. It checks inventory identifier uniqueness and nonnegative prices/quantities, and produces a material-term index without guessing unresolved matches. -ValidateOnly also rejects missing or stale generated maps; run generation after editing the source audits or inventory and include those maps in the change. It does not infer official alignment, substitute usability, safety, developmental appropriateness or classroom mastery from a passing schema.

The all-grade reference validator compares frozen baseline keys, requires a complete package for every selected lesson, checks actual local-code presence, contiguous native meeting intervals, class-size coverage and relative links. The band reviews retain the separate material-arithmetic/content desk checks. Structural validation is not an observed classroom trial.

docs.title: Substitute readiness review
docs.text:
October 2026. A revised template is not certification of every lesson. This workstream owns shared operations, not the four band lesson audits. Readiness requires a completed lesson, counted physical kit, accommodations, named local contact and successful prep test. Classroom outcomes, inventory condition, staff availability and school policies remain unverified.

Evidence status: The seven simulations below are planned desk walk-throughs of documents and assumptions. No substitute-arrival trial, pupil classroom test, observed teacher-prep timing or actual kit-capacity trial was performed. Future READY status requires the named local checks; it is not an outcome already established by this review.

Written-package closeout: all 251 current lesson documents are complete conditional references. The remaining release gate concerns actual kits, permissions, accommodations and trials, not a queue of missing outlines. See full verification and the school checklist.

docs.title: What changed in shared operations
docs.text: Baseline problems: the old substitute guide assumed nonexistent quick-reference cards and "likely" equipment locations, treated paper as an equivalent for programming, and had no complete classroom cleanup/evidence allocation. The updated substitute guide supplies the actual 20-minute gate, native-period fallback plans and safety escalation. The handoff template attaches a complete lesson plan, not a second format. Shared kits and actual stock assumptions live in Materials Plan.

docs.title: Grade 3, twenty minutes before class
docs.text:
Use this actual target, maintained by the band owner: Week 10: Bridge Engineering. Use the rebuilt lesson's exact span, loads, issue quantities and individual check; the generic structures kit is not permission to change those silently. Do not read its old title as proof of readiness.

Preparation window Substitute action Evidence of readiness 0-4 minutes Read the linked lesson's at-a-glance objective, background, misconception and 40-minute sequence Can state the objective and individual success condition 4-8 Locate the labeled kit and count actual enrollment; this bridge uses 12 active pair/trio teams at 25, with a 13-kit supply budget 26 books, 28 paper sheets, 260 identical counters, 13 cups/trays/team rulers, 5.2 m tape, 25 evidence slips and the specified teacher reserves are present 8-12 Review safety/accommodations; confirm office contact/stop procedure; inspect supports and loads No damaged/sharp/loose unsafe items; no hidden teacher-only task 12-16 Run the lesson's prep test and prepare trays/roles Test result is observable; setup can be safely supervised 16-20 Draw/read aloud steps; rehearse one exit prompt, return counts and fallback Individual roster and 40-minute cleanup/evidence allocation ready

If the exact kit/pretest is unavailable, explicitly teach the paper comparison fallback in the substitute guide instead. Tell the regular teacher which bridge objectives/evidence were deferred. The nine-team generic structures kit is not the complete pair-based bridge kit. The fallback uses groups of up to three and its own quantities and test, so record the changed objective rather than silently changing the bridge's span, loading method or team allocation. Do not add unsourced theological metaphors, ratio mathematics or unfamiliar electric equipment to rescue a lesson.

Readiness states: READY after local checks; CONDITIONAL with a named, tested support/fallback; NOT READY with unresolved safety, material, instruction or assessment blockers. The link and a document simulation do not establish school-wide READY status.

docs.title: Seven desk simulations (not classroom trials)
docs.text: Simulation Shared resources tested conceptually Outcome and limit 1. Substitute arrives 20 minutes before Grade 3 Linked rebuilt bridge target + gate above + structures kit/fallback Feasible only after actual kit/count/pretest; no blanket legacy certification 2. K child cannot read Show, Try, Tell, real objects, one modeled step and pointing/gesture No reading/writing prerequisite; teacher still records each child's concept evidence 3. iPads unavailable Technology Plan separates no-device concepts from execution Core works; software/robot execution deferred and NE, never programming mastery from paper 4. Minnesota January, -10 F Indoor desk observation, paper engineering, classroom comparison No outdoor exposure needed; a weather-specific outdoor objective requires a different approved lesson 5. Enrollment 25 Generic core: nine teams up to three; revised pair-based bridge: 12 active teams plus one reserve kit; seated work and 25 response opportunities Use the selected lesson's count, not one universal kit count; actual supplies and room layout still need checking 6. Budget ceiling $250 Goods $194 + tax $15.52 + shipping $10 + durable reserve $10 = $229.52 Hands-on low-tech core plus protected AA equipment; one cohort and existing basics assumed, not all legacy lessons 7. Parent asks what learning occurred Unit copy, objective-linked rubric, actual evidence and Catholic decision Teacher can give concept/action/evidence/next step; family tasks remain optional

docs.title: Required local checks before handoff
docs.text:
• Verify school contact/emergency arrangements, accommodations and actual kit shelf locations; this review invents none.
  • Verify protected electrical ratings, secure covers, age suitability, ingredients and counts. No button cells, latex balloons or projectiles; no neodymium magnets in K. Suspected battery/magnet ingestion requires immediate school emergency escalation.
  • Confirm the current rebuilt bridge instructions and physical kit agree. Band audits record document-level revision evidence, not classroom testing or official certification; this operations review does not replace them.
  • Reconcile the four available audit CSVs by lesson path; record substitute/safety/technology blockers. The Grade 3 band owner has documented the rebuilt bridge reference and conservative 13-kit supply budget; verify the actual local kit rather than using the earlier as-read snapshot. The audit is not classroom certification. All 251 packages passed the actual written-reference checks; do not infer physical classroom release merely because those document checks passed.
  • Check Local Standards definitions, faith sources and official alignment; unverified Church or supplier claims are VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

The substitute leaves actual individual evidence/NE, accomplished steps, objective changes, missing/broken supplies, safety issues and follow-up questions.

docs.title: Technology plan
docs.text: October 2026. Technology includes tools, systems, algorithms, input/output and ethical decisions, not only screens. Computer science is not synonymous with consuming an app. Actual school accounts, licenses, privacy approvals, device counts, Wi-Fi and loan availability are VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

docs.title: Four requirement labels
docs.text:
Label Meaning Appropriate example None No digital device needed for the stated objective Observe/model/measure; compose a body-percussion phrase; follow and debug a paper algorithm Optional Device changes convenience, not the demonstrated objective Teacher photographs a model instead of drawing; optional document camera with real-object demonstration alternative Recommended Device adds educational value but the same objective can still be evidenced without it Large data set graphing when a manageable paper data set preserves the taught interpretation criterion Required Stated objective cannot be demonstrated without the actual digital/programmable device Run/debug a Scratch program; operate a programmed robot or sensor; test an interactive input controller

Each lesson names the device/app version, compatible access, why it is needed, quantity/turns, prep test and fallback. Electricity using protected AA packs does not require a screen. Digital art is not the only arts route: observational drawing, model form, composition, rhythm and performance are authentic A.

docs.title: Objective-preserving vs objective-changing alternatives
docs.text:
Learning purpose Usual label No-device route Evidence limit Sequence, loops, conditions, decomposition, debugging concepts None Large arrow cards, desk grids, repeated actions or sorting rules Evidence of computational thinking; not proof that software executed Closed path/input-output in simple circuits None Preflight-approved Snap Circuits in selected OLP lessons, or the separate protected-AA route Paper circuit diagram alone does not prove building/testing an electrical circuit Science observation, temperature, structures, measurement None Physical objects, non-glass tools, individual show/tell/data A teacher demo alone does not evidence every student's investigation Observation/composition/pattern/music objective None or Optional Paper design and sound/silence phrase with body percussion If objective specifically concerns a digital tool, paper changes it Evidence documentation/presentation Optional Draw/label/model/orally explain Personal recording devices are not prerequisites Research/data interpretation Recommended only with justification Teacher-vetted printed/text read-aloud source; small supplied data set Online source-evaluation objective requires appropriate actual online examples/access Scratch/ScratchJr executable program Required Plan/trace/debug on paper now; schedule executable program later Mark execution objective NE/deferred; never record programming mastery from paper Dash/Sphero/Ozobot or sensor-controlled behavior Required Predict/trace algorithm using pointer on grid Robot operation, sensing and live debugging require working compatible equipment later Standalone stored-program floor robot Required for execution Large paper sequence while unit is unavailable Optional enhanced purchase; no host assumed only after product verification USB input/Makey Makey/modular app-linked project Required where digital response is O1 Draw input/output model or use AA circuit for a different O1 Different objective explicitly recorded; proprietary power components never improvised

If the technology fails: try the lesson's pretested basic restart/connection steps briefly, then protect teaching time and switch to a named fallback. Do not create personal accounts, bypass protections, install unknown software or download unapproved materials during class. Record what objective changed, what was actually demonstrated and when the missing evidence will be collected.

docs.title: Access, capacity and sustainability
docs.text:
Default maximum team size three: 10/15/20/25 pupils need ⅘/7/9 working team devices. Each student needs an execution/debugging turn for individual evidence. If there are only four devices for 25, plan nine teams in three rotations, each with a specified test/reset time and meaningful non-device work; schedule additional meetings if native 25/30/40/45 minutes cannot include every turn, assessment and cleanup. Do not equate watching another group with mastery. Account accessibility and sensory/motor supports must be confirmed.

The materials budgets fund no managed tablet/computer or licensed app. Enhanced robots are a conditional option, not a promise of Dash/Sphero/EV3 availability. HOST/DASH/SPHERO/MODULAR/INPUT database rows are legacy inventory questions. Verify loan contents, dates, chargers, missing pieces, age ratings, host compatibility, app availability/support and all fees before selecting a device-dependent lesson.

docs.title: Before any app or online service
docs.text:
Verification required Responsible school role to assign Evidence to retain locally Existing managed device count/condition, chargers, compatible OS [Technology lead] Asset count and dated trial Cost/free license terms, education eligibility, offline capability [Purchasing/technology lead] Current vendor terms and tested function Age terms, accounts, data collected, retention/deletion, consent [Administrator/privacy lead] Actual approval under school policy Access restrictions, advertisements, public sharing and accessibility [Teacher/technology lead] Classroom configuration and fallback Student images/names/work and family permission [School-approved contact] Verified school consent process, not assumed consent Loan inventory and return/transportation terms [Loan coordinator] Confirmed booking, complete kit and dates

Scratch, ScratchJr, Code.org, Chrome Music Lab, Canva, Tinkercad and robot apps are legacy candidates, not guaranteed free/approved/installed services. Use current vendor information for verification; this plan creates no school account or privacy policy. No student data are uploaded as part of this review.

docs.title: All-grade audit reconciliation
docs.text:
The final October 4 integration of all four band audits classifies 251 document records as 198 None, 12 Optional, 10 Recommended, 31 Required. K has 0 Required; grades 1-2 have 10, grades 3-4 have 15 and grades 5-6 have 6. These are primary-path audit labels, not meeting counts, ownership or readiness certifications. Protected AA circuit materials remain required even when the digital-technology label is None. Use the generated lesson map for subsequent updates.

Use actual paths, schedules and rotations to connect material/host questions. Keep objective-preserving and objective-changing fallback fields distinct. Recorded devices/kit names indicate procurement questions, not ownership, approval or safe equivalent substitution. Confirm Ozobot/EV3/other proprietary platforms separately rather than pricing them as the generic floor robot. All 251 written packages are complete. Actual app/device inventory, licenses, compatibility, local release and observed outcomes remain unverified. No school holding is inferred from a name or an access resource.

OLP Snap follow-up: the school confirmed eight individual activity kits, not classroom packs. The classroom guide documents four selected lesson pathways, matching-model/age/power gates, five-station/two-wave access at 25 pupils and separate physical/paper evidence. Snap's slide switch uses two states repeated twice; it does not establish the protected-AA push-button route's four independently controlled states. No computer/app is added, and no unverified holder equivalence is claimed.

Operational entry points: library planning, substitute guide, lesson template. Standards claims use Local Standards; official alignment requires verification.

docs.title: Completion checks and seven classroom simulations
docs.text: Review/completion work: October 4, 2026. Evidence is document inspection, source verification, arithmetic and desk walkthroughs. No actual classroom, substitute-arrival, physical-kit or student-outcome trial was performed.

docs.title: Current curriculum result
docs.text:
All 251 lesson documents now have complete conditional teaching packages:

Band Documents Planned meetings across alternatives Native minutes K 37 49 25 1-2 74 98 30 3-4 71 99 40 5-6 69 99 45 Total library 251 345 Grade-specific

These are alternative schedules/rotations, not one child's annual dose. Each pupil follows one selected track. The scope and band reviews distinguish teaching meetings, calendar breaks and file counts.

  • Shared reference validation passed 345 contiguous native-period meetings, 2,002 numbered intervals and 266 relative lesson links.
  • Every lesson's local codes appear in its instructions and connect to planned individual evidence. The current map has 929 local-standard evidence links.
  • All original audit dispositions/priorities, paths and meeting allocations remain separate from revision state. 251 rebuilt, 0 improved-only, 0 unchanged packages is document completion, not safety certification.
  • The source register retains 18 local competencies, 126 grade targets and 126 planned progression-stage entries.
  • Current material/resource/catalog totals are in Program Summary and planned use, not guessed from old snapshots. Physical items, access resources, kit components and reported stock remain distinct.

Final identity reconciliation covers 2,158 occurrences: 1,965 physical catalog names, 189 resource/component references and four reported-stock references, across 114 catalogue identities and 32 declared resources. Zero unresolved term identities remain. Exact product specifications, measured mass, safe condition and ownership are still local checks, not automatic consequences of matching a name.

The final early-grade context handoff also records exact role boundaries: twenty approximately 2 cm equal units per Pi team, two different-sized lids, one 30 cm flexible ruler per sound team with 8/14 cm free lengths, two 60 cm yarn pieces, and two identical permanently sealed teacher-prepared rice shakers per class with explicit no-shaker alternatives. Cataloguing does not invent a commercial shaker, cotton/nonstretch guarantee, pot capacity from mix volume, spoon magnetism or interchangeable hand-span units.

docs.title: Verification controls
docs.text:
Check What it establishes What it does not establish Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1 -ValidateOnly Complete audit/header/enums, unique paths, native periods/codes, full 24-field catalog, valid counts, explicit resource identities and fresh generated maps Real school stock, compatible product, safe inspected equipment or student mastery Test-LessonReferences.ps1 All packages complete, baseline keys unchanged, required teaching/evidence sections, every local code present, contiguous times and existing relative targets Observed teacher pacing, semantic mastery or formal subject approval Test-KindergartenReferences.ps1 29 autonomous references, 37 new native meetings and 360 scalable quantity comparisons; all 37 K records complete Actual seed growth, wet-area capacity or classroom outcomes Band-owner arithmetic/content checks 2,636 early-grade supply cells, 956 middle-grade comparisons, 1,172 upper-grade comparisons and explicit worked/model/evidence boundaries Vendor quotations, physical condition or outcome studies Test-SnapCircuitsReferences.ps1 Four retained paths, six native meetings, 20 station/capacity rows, eight reported individual kits and physical/paper evidence boundaries Manufacturer model/age/power approval or kit inspection Test-CurriculumMaps.ps1 Physical/resource/holding output shapes, empty-backlog behavior and 15 rejection cases, including malformed inventory and stale maps Approval inferred from a structurally valid row Test-MaterialsBudget.ps1 Original 37-row bills, four ceilings/year-two calculations and generic team capacities Actual prices/stock or purchase coverage for all alternatives Build-ExternalAlignment.ps1 -ValidateOnly 29 exact candidates, 16 used identifiers, 26 lesson paths; source/grade/locator/scope/status checks against 24 verified benchmark records Full subject coverage, institutional approval or observed mastery

Original first-year configurations remain $229.52 / $476.04 / $854.32 / $2,367.84. The first three assume one cohort and existing school basics; enhanced consumables assume seven sequential cohorts. Additional catalog identities are not silently added to those purchase bills. Costs remain estimates.

docs.title: Source completion and limits
docs.text:
• Direct source inspection verified sixteen state-agency 2018 arts identifiers/ grades and eight current national CSTA 2026 identifiers/boundaries.
  • Proposed external rows match actual written tasks and planned evidence. Partial algorithms, art choices or software demonstrations are not upgraded into full benchmark mastery.
  • State-agency arts copies retain MDE-copy corroboration/school review. National CSTA publication does not establish Minnesota/diocesan adoption.
  • Normal final MDE science/math and other document retrieval returned browser-verification pages; no inaccessible table or guessed code is published.
  • Four Catholic heritage cards use directly inspected institutional/scholarly facts, not fabricated quotes, unsupported motivations or sole-discovery claims.

docs.title: Seven required simulations
docs.text: Simulation Concrete written pathway and correction Desk result and remaining local check 1. Substitute arrives 20 minutes before Grade 3 Bridge Engineering has a 40-minute sequence, pretest, fair load method and individual evidence. Handoff uses its conservative 13-kit allocation rather than nine generic kits. Conditional pass with prepared kit; check real location, counts, room, accommodations and pretest. Use the named different fallback if unavailable and record deferred objectives. 2. K child cannot read All K minimum pathways use oral/picture modeling, pointing/dictation and child-directed manipulation. K routines define actual pair/trio turns. Document pass; reading/handwriting not prerequisites. Actual access needs and individual evidence still require teacher observation. 3. iPads unavailable Every lesson identifies its primary requirement and named fallback. Algorithms/models remain distinct from real execution/operation. Local low-tech learning continues; required software/robot/sensor operation is deferred, not falsely awarded from paper or watching. 4. Minnesota January, -10 F All reference packages state indoor routes; actual/supplied/model weather observations are labeled. Growth/care and wet cleanup are explicit. Document pass for indoor learning; do not report model data as measured weather. School plant care, hygiene and room conditions still need checks. 5. Enrollment reaches 25 Exact class-size allocations, role turns and concurrent checks replace serial queues. Generic groups use seven trios/two pairs; pair-based lessons keep their larger kit budget. Snap uses bounded station/wave plans. Arithmetic/logistics pass; real room, inspection throughput, supplies and processing needs are untested. Unobserved evidence remains unobserved. 6. Limited funding Modest no-device core and reusable kits; purchase ceilings verified without assuming donations/loans or all specialty gear. Conditional budget pass; verify stock/prices/specifications and the chosen track's consumption. Safe procurement is not improvised to preserve a price. 7. Parent asks what is learned Each reference has family copy, an objective/evidence threshold and grade support/challenge. Progression and maps explain increasing sophistication. Document pass; explain what actually happened and was demonstrated, not just planned targets or group participation. Home invitations remain optional.

docs.title: Changes made to close the remaining document backlog
docs.text:
1. Rebuilt all remaining Grades 1-6 packages, preserving earlier references and the updated Snap routes; no audit-only or incomplete outline is labeled complete.
  2. Added actual individual checks, worked/fictional data and scientific/model limits; removed withdrawn unsafe paths and unsupported heritage quotations.
  3. Preserved realistic periods and includes cleanup, setup, trial/role plans, scalable supplies, troubleshooting and younger/older grade expectations.
  4. Reconciled material names without pretending software, a saved record, a module or reported holding is an independently verified purchase.
  5. Added exact external-candidate validation and a frozen baseline ledger.
  6. Moved map regression, all-grade reference, budget, K, Snap and source-map checks into publication CI; pull requests validate/build without deployment.
  7. Explicitly excluded the documentation-root developer README from publication, resolving the earlier README/index conflict so the build can run strictly.

docs.title: Remaining work is school-specific release evidence
docs.text:
No written lesson-package backlog remains. The school release checklist requires actual counts/condition, model/manual/power checks, source/policy approval, individual accommodations, prepared content, physical kit locations and classroom pilots. Source access limitations are recorded, not "fixed" by unsupported official claims.

Before asserting uniformly classroom-ready delivery, pilot selected lessons, time actual preparation/cleanup and collect individual evidence at the local checkpoints. A full document or a passing schema cannot perform those checks. Unresolved unsafe conditions hold the affected pathway; a changed fallback records changed/deferred objectives.
